copy_review.evidence:
Installation working paper, revision A. This paper records decisions made at today's planning meeting; it is not a completion certificate. We divided the installation into a mechanical workstream, a visitor information workstream, and a packing workstream. The mechanical team owns the anchor survey and motor connection. The education team owns the wall label and a large-print handout. The registrar owns the crate inventory and the condition photographs. A completed item in one workstream must not close an item in another.

The proposed packing list has three numbered pieces. Piece P1 is the suspended sculpture body, P2 is the detached counterweight, and P3 is the motor enclosure. The plinth is gallery equipment and must not be added as a shipped fourth sculpture piece. Each packing photograph needs both the piece number and a view of its support foam. We have photographs of the empty crate interior, but not photographs showing the pieces packed. The registrar therefore left the packing-evidence column open.

For the label, the education team requested a short description of the motion, a materials line, and a plain-language explanation of why the sculpture is stationary when the motor is off. The artist's draft description calls the motion continuous, while the technician's planning note says demonstrations may be intermittent. We have asked the artist to resolve that wording. No editor may silently turn the planning note into an approved artistic description. The school handout can describe the visible shape without settling that issue.

The floor-plan sketch marks a visitor waiting rectangle, a technician working rectangle and an unassigned buffer between them. These are drawing annotations, not taped boundaries on the gallery floor. The accessibility coordinator asked for a photograph from a seated viewing position after installation. There is no photograph yet and no accessibility sign-off. The coat rack was suggested as a possible waiting-area reference but has not been chosen.

The crate supplier asked whether the counterweight needs a separate sleeve. The registrar will ask the artist before ordering one. A sleeve order, if approved, would be recorded in the packing workstream. The next meeting should review the piece list and the two competing motion descriptions, not assume that a purchase or installation has already taken place.

copy_review.evidence:
Installation working paper, revision B. The technician added the mandatory anchor inspection to the mechanical workstream today. It is a prerequisite for powering the motor and is not replaced by the fact that the plinth has been measured. The inspection entry needs the inspector's name, date and scope. At present all three spaces are blank. We can schedule other work around that open entry, but we cannot fill it with the name of a person who merely discussed the installation.

The registrar compared the artist's packing sketch with revision A. The detached counterweight needs its own foam sleeve, but remains piece P2 rather than becoming a new numbered object. The artist approved asking for a price; approval to request a price is not approval to place an order. The supplier has not provided that price. We left the purchase-status box empty and placed a request in the questions list. P1 and P3 still use the supports shown on the original sketch.

The label draft was printed for layout review this morning. It contains the materials line but leaves a bracketed space where the disputed motion description will go. The printer's proof includes the word DRAFT in its margin. The artist's signature line is blank. A volunteer offered to trim the margin to make the proof look finished; the education lead declined because that would obscure its review status. The printed proof should remain available for comments, not be mounted as the finished label.

The education team proposed an accompanying large-print sheet. It would repeat the final approved label, then add a diagram showing the three visible parts. The diagram can be drawn now, but its caption must wait for the motion wording. We assigned the diagram to the illustrator and the text check to the education lead. These assignments are proposed task ownership, not evidence that either task has been done.

The courier asked for total packed dimensions before selecting a vehicle. The registrar can supply crate dimensions but has not measured the packed piece arrangement. We will answer with the known crate dimensions and explicitly identify the missing measurement. We will not choose a vehicle merely because another exhibition used one of the same size. Next steps remain a sleeve price request, a diagram draft and a packing measurement.

The anchor entry therefore remains open, and the trial photographs should be stored under lighting evidence rather than in the inspection folder.

The registrar completed the P1 and P3 packing photographs. Each image shows the correct number and support foam. The three-piece photo set is now complete. The packed arrangement was measured and added to the courier attachment. The courier note is still unsent pending the gallery manager's review of the complete package.

The education lead accepted the artist's proposed phrase about scheduled demonstrations as consistent with the operating plan. The artist still needs to sign the resulting clean label proof. We have two text files: the earlier commented proof and the clean proof incorporating the accepted wording. The inventory lists four spare bulbs in the maintenance box. It does not list four mounted light fixtures. The completed photographs and measurements should not be unnecessarily commissioned again.

The gallery manager asked staff to retain the photograph showing ordinary coats in the recess, because it explains the conditions under which the waiting-area choice was approved.

Neither requires inventing a motor test or restarting completed packing photographs. Keep the maintenance sheet's spare-bulb count distinct from installed fixtures. The draft strip can say the amber lot tested at eighty percent germination; it must not imply a second test.

Seed-bank intake and release ledger, edition A. We have three independent records for this cycle: a tray-observation sheet, a packet-preparation sheet and a school-request sheet. They share a lot identifier but serve different purposes. A number of packets on a shelf is not the number of seeds in a trial, and an expression of interest from a school is not a dispatch. The coordinator asked us to keep those distinctions visible in every later handoff.

The amber lot observation sheet records twenty seeds placed in the first tray and sixteen marked sprouted at the reading. These two counts describe that tray only. Four positions were marked not sprouted at that reading; the sheet does not say those seeds could never sprout. No second tray was measured and no combined result is available. The violet lot remains untested. Do not use the amber tray as evidence about the violet seeds simply because the packets will use similar envelopes.

The packet-preparation team has an amber envelope mock-up with spaces for the lot identifier, packing date and an enclosure check. The mock-up is not an approved package. A volunteer proposed printing a large garden illustration over the whole front. The coordinator asked the volunteer to leave the lot identifier readable and to return a revised design. The illustration is a design proposal, not a statement about the variety inside.

The request sheet lists Hill School as asking about a classroom demonstration and Orchard School as asking about a spring garden session. Neither has confirmed a delivery date. We asked each school to name a receiving teacher and indicate whether it can store packets in a dry cupboard. These questions concern readiness to receive materials; they do not change the contents or the test report of a seed lot.

We assigned the envelope proof to the packing lead and the teacher contacts to the outreach lead. The empty trays were washed, but no new seeds have been planted. The next meeting should resolve the envelope proof and collect the missing school contacts. It should not invent a second trial merely to fill an empty column or describe the untested violet lot as equivalent to amber. Keep the counts on the tray sheet attached to their original lot and reading.

Reservation administration note, edition A. The laser-level reservation and the hammer booking are separate entries with different borrowers. The counter volunteer will prepare a handoff packet for each, rather than combine them because both tools are used for home repairs. The laser-level packet currently contains a reservation sheet and a visual-condition checklist. The visual check found no obvious external damage, but does not establish calibration accuracy or substitute for the instrument's calibration card.

The storage worksheet uses plant names for lockers and numbers for the shelves inside each locker. The laser-level reservation belongs to Locker Birch, shelf two. Shelf two alone is not a complete location, because several lockers have a second shelf. The carrying case should remain associated with its reservation identifier. A copy of the storage worksheet that preserves both the locker name and the reservation mapping carries the same location information as the main reservation sheet, even if it is called an inventory aid.

The accessories list has three entries: the carrying case, a battery pack and a small mounting bracket. The volunteer has counted the case and battery but has not checked the bracket compartment. The checklist should mark the bracket count pending. We do not have evidence that the bracket is missing; an unchecked compartment is not a loss report. The borrower has not collected the tool, so no return condition can be recorded.

A deposit has been paid for the reservation, and reception must issue a receipt. The receipt needs the reservation identifier and the recorded payment date; it does not need the locker assignment. The finance volunteer proposed a reusable receipt template but has not tested whether it prints the identifier clearly. We will prepare a sample before printing the borrower's actual receipt. This is an administrative formatting task, not a request for a second payment.

The tool library is also considering a short orientation for new borrowers on checking accessories before departure. A volunteer offered a draft outline, but no session is scheduled. The next coordinator should keep this proposal separate from the individual reservation. Immediate tasks are checking the bracket compartment, testing the receipt template and locating the correct instrument card. None is evidence that pickup has happened or that the future orientation has been delivered.

The draft route note sends the Gannet team to the upstream willow bridge.

Fieldwork planning ledger, issue A. We are maintaining separate records for Gannet field preparation, Heron laboratory checks and a school demonstration. Gannet is the instrument assigned to the stream trip. Heron is the laboratory device. Charging both loggers does not make their purposes interchangeable, and a file produced by one must not be described as evidence about the other. The case labels should show the instrument identifier before any equipment leaves the preparation room.

The local route sketch uses N1 as a shorthand stop code. Its legend defines N1 as the upstream willow bridge, and the Gannet trip row selects N1. The code is not a different site. A note combining the trip row with the legend can reconstruct the same site assignment even if it omits the words from the main field. We have not surveyed a route or sent a team out merely by creating this planning sketch.

The equipment checklist has a transport case, a label camera, spare logger batteries and a printed field form. The transport case has been ordered but has not arrived. The camera is available, although its battery has not been charged. The printed form exists as a draft with blank spaces for instrument identity, condition and deployment time. Blank spaces must not be filled from planned dates. The final field observations will need their own record.

Heron will be checked in a bucket in the laboratory. The technician proposed collecting a short file and checking whether its sample intervals are regular. No test has run yet. The team should record both a file name and the instrument identifier when the test occurs, because a generic name such as trial-one can easily be mistaken for a field deployment file. We asked for a naming convention before the first test.

The school has requested a demonstration but has not chosen a location. The education lead suggested either the courtyard or a classroom table. This is a separate activity with different safety and supervision needs from field deployment. The next meeting should settle a device-specific file naming convention, confirm the transport case receipt and choose a demonstration format. None of those decisions establishes field data, a permit signature or a completed stream trip.

Tactile-map production ledger, draft A. This project has a raised campus map, a separate wall poster and a companion-document package. The wall poster may use color and visual symbols that are unsuitable for a touch-readable surface. We therefore assigned each product its own proof identifier and review checklist. A decision about poster background color must not silently change the raised-map specification or stand in for a tactile readability test.

The first raised-map proof sheet contains a calibration example: one centimetre on the sheet represents twenty metres on the campus plan. That example encodes the same scale as the first reported proof specification. It is not a second independent measurement. The sheet labels the example reference bar, so the comparison must not be confused with the physical width of a raised path line. Later notes should preserve which number describes scale and which describes line construction.

The route inventory includes the north entrance, library path, garden junction and courtyard ramp. We collected these names from the project's fictional campus plan; no claim about a real campus is intended. The names are not yet approved for the companion document. The education team asked whether library path should instead be called library approach to match the sign text. That naming question is unresolved and must not be settled by a designer's preference alone.

The tactile designer proposed three symbol families: a solid dot for a destination, a double line for a main path and a crosshatched square for a restricted work area. These are draft symbols. We have not tested whether readers can distinguish them by touch, and we do not have participant feedback. The designer will prepare a small symbol sample sheet before committing the full map to production.

The wall-poster designer suggested a pale background and a large title. The education lead asked for a visual contrast proof but has not approved the proposal. The project also needs a clear way to package the raised map with its companion material, so the registrar will sketch an envelope that does not crush the raised features. Next tasks are resolving route names, preparing symbol samples and evaluating the package concept. None is evidence that the full map has passed a user trial or that a complete distribution set exists.

We drafted a volunteer trial plan with three activities: identify a destination, trace a path between two named points and locate the companion legend. A mock-up that protects the map can still fail the identification task, so these observations need separate checklist rows.

The wall-poster designer has not delivered the contrast proof. The team should not delay route-name corrections while waiting for that independent visual product. A useful next handoff names the accepted spellings, the untested tactile sample, the revised sleeve requirement and the pending room check. The existence of a trial plan does not establish recruitment, attendance or measured performance, and the package mock-up is not a finished distribution envelope.

Design decision and trial update. The building closed the reserved room, so the volunteer trial was postponed before recruitment. There are no participant observations, timing results or comments to summarize. The coordinator will seek a new room rather than report the trial as failed. The design team approved the smoother raised border as a future revision. The border has not been printed on the full map. The crosshatched work-area symbol remains distinct in the draft set, and the legend text may need a small addition describing the newly approved border. The education lead asked the writer to prepare that addition, but it is not yet reviewed. Approval of a design change does not automatically update every dependent companion file.

The campus path list now includes the garden ramp. The map designer marked its proposed placement on a revision drawing, while the education team drafted a name entry for the companion sheet. The team has not printed the revised map. The added route is a content update, not evidence about the disputed first proof scale. We will keep the revision drawing and the original proof separate so a later reader can tell which features belong to which version.

The registrar tested a shorter envelope flap. It no longer presses on the raised sample edge and preserves the visible identifier tab. The package concept is now accepted for a small production order, but the order has not been placed. The team should not continue listing the long-flap problem as unresolved after this accepted test. It should instead record the new pending step of ordering the approved envelope design.

The ruler discrepancy remains unresolved and no corrected scale has been established. A useful next coordinator action is to obtain review of the border addition and garden-ramp entry before printing companion sheets, while separately arranging the approved packaging order. These tasks do not require pretending the postponed trial happened or treating the new drawing as a measured replacement proof. Preserve both the accepted design decisions and their incomplete downstream document updates.

The next handoff should ask the printer to identify the returned sheet, track the packaging delivery and preserve the printed legend master's version. Route spelling, poster color and the short-flap design are resolved. The print-scale discrepancy, unlabeled proof and user trial are not. A practical task can advance the packaging and identifier checks without claiming any corrected scale, approving an unknown proof or pairing a legend with a map whose revision has not been established.

Rehearsal office workbook. The caption team is opening three small work streams alongside the room booking: cue-file control, equipment readiness, and a pack for a substitute operator. The printed cue list is the working draft. The cue writer proposes adding a revision line to the top of every page so a loose page can be matched to the file that produced it. That change has not been made yet. The team has not assigned a revision number to the printed copy and should preserve it as the initial working print rather than guessing its version.

For equipment, the stage manager proposes separate rows for the main laptop, backup laptop, power supplies, and display connection. A successful test of one device would close only that device's row. The manager wants the test note to say which file was opened and what action was tried, because a machine that starts is not necessarily ready to display captions. No laptop test is recorded in this opening entry. The proposed inventory can be completed without changing the rehearsal room or the dancers' separate booking.

The substitute-operator pack is intended to explain how to find the current cue list and how to ask the stage manager about an unclear cue. It will not be a public announcement. The coordinator has drafted two possible pack layouts: a chronological cue index or a short task sheet with links to the relevant cue sections. A substitute has not reviewed either layout. The next office task is to ask which format would help someone stepping in for one rehearsal without reading the entire script first.

The workbook has separate spaces for completed work, decisions, and open questions. The initial completed item is the printed draft list. The proposed revision header, equipment rows, and pack formats are still work to do or choices to make. The coordinator will use the next session to establish the stage requirements before committing to a pack layout. This keeps the office from polishing instructions around assumptions that the production has not yet approved. The opening record supplies the plan and its dependencies; it does not claim a rehearsal, device test, or substitute briefing has occurred.

The office has assigned the cue change log to writer Inez and the device worksheet to stage assistant Bo. The coordinator will combine their notes only at handoff. A combined packet should retain each author's observation so a later equipment exception is not mistaken for a text decision made by the writer.

copy_review.evidence:
Lesson planning record. The class is creating a result sheet, a course map, and a notebook for changes to the robot program. These will be separate documents because they answer different questions. The result sheet records what a trial report says. The map identifies the physical course used. The program notebook records which code was prepared or changed. A shared heading will link the documents to the lesson without suggesting that every robot has already completed every activity.

The teacher has drafted a result-table layout with columns for robot name, trial identifier, reported result, and observation notes. A blank cell will mean missing information rather than zero. The draft still needs student review. The teacher wants to know whether a reader can distinguish a reported measurement from an empty row for a robot that has not run. The first review will use paper examples, not another timed run. No aggregate statistic will be calculated until the class has an appropriate set of measurements.

For the course map, the students have drawn an outline showing the assembled barriers and the proposed route. They have not measured the full path. The map has a space for a key explaining barrier labels, but the barriers do not yet carry those labels. The next map task is to agree a labeling scheme and decide how to show measured and unmeasured sections. A drawing may help plan the work without proving that its scale is correct.

The program notebook starts with a proposed naming rule: save a copy before changing a motion instruction, then write a short reason for the change. The class has not adopted the rule yet. The teacher proposes using a dry code review to compare two possible turn instructions without moving a robot. That review can proceed alongside the table and map work. The next session should select the document conventions before students create more versions. The lesson is not a competition between the robots at this stage; there is no comparable result for the unrun robot. This opening record supplies the paperwork plan and leaves the proposed reviews, measurements, and code discussion as future classroom tasks.

The teacher assigned the map notebook to the route group and the result-sheet layout to the evidence group. A third code group will own program notes. Each group will name its author on a submitted page so a later correction can be directed to the group with the relevant evidence rather than guessed from handwriting.

Document conventions and preparation checklist. The students reviewed the draft result table and asked for a status column. The teacher has added the choices reported, missing, and under review, with a note that a status describes the evidence rather than robot performance. An empty numeric cell remains empty. The class will not use a dash and zero interchangeably, because that would make a missing measurement look like a result. The revised table is ready for a paper exercise using the existing report.

The course map will use letters for barriers and a dashed line for any unmeasured path segment. This is a drafting convention, not a completed labeling task. The students will measure sections in small groups and record which segment each observation covers. The teacher has added the cable-clearance condition to the preparation checklist before any further timed run, while leaving actual clearance unconfirmed.

The program naming proposal is adopted. A student making a change should preserve the earlier file, name the new version, and describe the reason in the notebook. The first dry review will compare a broad turn instruction with a more gradual sequence, but no revised code has been loaded. The possible ramp-angle change is another proposal and belongs in the course change log rather than the program notebook. Keeping those logs separate will help the class explain whether a future difference came from code, course geometry, or neither.

The charged spare battery has its own preparation entry. It does not settle the timing evidence or show that a robot is ready for another run. The teacher asks the next session to bring the partial map measurements, the paper-table exercise, and the dry-review notes. Each group should identify what it actually checked and what remains open. The next class can then choose which task to advance without inventing a complete map or an additional trial. This documentation work is useful even if the robot stays on its stand, since it improves how later observations will be connected to the conditions under which they were made.

The evidence group chose a blue header for form instructions and a plain header for entered observations. The choice is a visual aid, not an evidence status. The teacher asked that every status also be written in words so a monochrome print remains interpretable when the class reviews the sheet later.

existing_copy_edges.basis:
Internal communications packet, version C1. The draft arrival note is addressed to the lantern crew and says to assemble in the western yard beside the orchard. That wording refers to the same staging assignment recorded in the opening conversation, not a second site. The packet has no public-list release. The coordinator has kept the recipient field separate from the subject line because a general festival subject does not make every detail suitable for every audience. A volunteer may prepare a cover message for review, but the document should remain an internal draft until its permitted distribution is established.

The decoration review has rejected the paper-tassel proposal because of the risk of catching on hinges. The proposal sheet has been moved to the rejected section with the reason attached. There is no installation record to reverse: the tassels were proposed, not fitted. The art volunteer has instead offered to make a printed illustration for the programme. That is a new suggestion for a different product, and the coordinator has not yet accepted it. The programme suggestion must not be treated as a revived instruction to attach decoration to the frames.

Issue H1 is still open. The communications packet includes a reminder that a technician's response is needed, but it does not describe the hinge as repaired. The desk has also requested the original inventory worksheet to resolve the unclear entry. Until it arrives, the existing count fields should be carried forward with their status rather than silently replaced by a plausible number. The checklist editor can finish page layout while these facts remain unsettled.

The volunteer availability sheet now records two people who could carry a frame during a supervised trial. They have not agreed to act as supervisor, and their offers do not establish a trial booking. The next coordinator should seek an appropriately assigned supervisor, reconcile the inventory source and collect the hinge assessment. If preparing an outward-facing message, the coordinator can describe general preparation status without copying the crew arrival detail. Any use of the internal location field remains subject to the applicable access rules. This packet records communications and open work, not a completed gate passage or a confirmed public procession.
The C1 draft directs this crew to the orchard-side yard on the west. It remains internal and unsent; the tassel proposal is rejected.

copy_review.evidence:
Crew workbook, opening inventory. We have assembled the empty frames and attached temporary tags to them. The first spreadsheet has thirteen rows. Treat that as the number of entries on the sheet, not a verified count of different frames: the workshop has not reconciled the tags against the rows. Each row has spaces for tag, assembly status, light-module assignment and movement check. The movement-check spaces are empty. The sheet belongs to the lantern workshop; the indoor music crew keeps a separate equipment list and has not supplied it for this inventory.

We have introduced a three-pocket folder for the coming shifts. The first pocket holds physical-item records, the second holds proposals, and the third holds communications with separate draft and issued tabs. A draft communication stays under the draft tab until its sender records its intended audience and release. This is a filing choice for the fictional festival preparations. The folder does not itself approve a movement procedure or establish access to another crew's records. The desk has asked each volunteer to write an item tag on loose worksheets so that a later shift can distinguish an observation about one frame from a general instruction.

The initial planning board has three parallel work streams. The frame team will reconcile the inventory and inspect moving parts. The lighting team will identify which modules can be matched to which frames. The coordination team will collect volunteer availability for a supervised trial. A volunteer's availability is not a booking, and no supervisor has yet accepted a trial session. Two volunteers have offered to prepare a checklist, but we have not selected its final format. One suggests a single page per frame; the other suggests a shared table with a separate issue log.

The workshop has not yet decided on decorations. A sample envelope contains paper offcuts for discussion; nothing in that envelope has been approved for attachment. The next shift should keep the samples separate from assembled parts and ask the teams to return their missing information. Its handoff should distinguish the thirteen spreadsheet entries, the unverified physical count and the unfilled trial arrangements. That separation will allow clerical preparation to continue without presenting the event as ready for public operation.

Movement checklist draft, version M1. The gate procedure now requires each frame's projecting handles to be folded and secured before that frame is carried through. The workshop wants the trial record to identify the particular frame, the people carrying it and the supervising person, so a result for one frame cannot silently become a result for the entire inventory.

The lighting team has confirmed that the modules use batteries. Its preparation sheet asks for module identification and a place to record a bench test; the test-result fields are not yet completed. The inventory remains unreconciled. The first sheet still contains thirteen entries, and the desk has not counted unique tags. copy_review.reason: Repair color scheme and unapproved voucher reuse are separate procedural facts.
copy_review.evidence: For the repair tickets, use red for diagnosis pending, amber for repair complete but awaiting a second mechanic, and green for independently checked. A volunteer suggested using the same colors for vouchers. I have not approved that: a green repair ticket could otherwise look like permission to reimburse. I will print word labels for the voucher stages instead.

copy_review.reason: Voucher stage labels do not establish donation count.
copy_review.evidence: Using words for voucher stages avoids that accidental equivalence. Suggested labels are evidence needed, review ready, approved, and paid. A ticket may be green while its associated voucher is still evidence needed. Record the label decision separately from whether labels have actually been printed or attached.

copy_review.reason: Shared pump and open trolley booking plus a value-free undelivered-donation reference; no count.
copy_review.evidence: The venue gives us one shared hand pump and a narrow storage alcove. The volunteer desk needs a trolley for moving the paperwork box and tools; that booking is still open. Please include a setup section in the coordination notebook, but do not make tool availability depend on a donation that has not arrived. We can run inspection and minor adjustment stations with the equipment already checked in.

copy_review.reason: Three workstreams and unbooked trolley do not reconstruct twelve.
copy_review.evidence: I have separated three workstreams in the notebook: voucher evidence, repair verification, and venue setup. The trolley remains unbooked, the hand pump is shared, and the existing tools support inspection work. A later delivery must be logged as a new stock event rather than inferred from the pledge.

copy_review.reason: V12 purchase versus collection date discrepancy is unrelated to donation quantity.
copy_review.evidence: I unfolded V12 and scanned its receipt. The adhesive description is readable, but the date printed by the shop is one day earlier than the volunteer wrote on the voucher. The volunteer says she entered the collection day, not the purchase day. I have not rejected the claim. I want a short correction note showing both dates and why they differ, so the discrepancy remains visible rather than being erased from the scan.

copy_review.reason: Keep both dates and scan; no pledge content.
copy_review.evidence: Keep the scan unchanged and attach the volunteer's explanation to V12. The purchase date belongs in the expense-date field; collection day can remain in the note. A date mismatch with an explanation is different from missing proof of payment, and the reviewer should decide after seeing both.

copy_review.reason: V11 eligibility check and pending second reviewer give no donation count.
copy_review.evidence: V11 passed the basic eligibility check today. I have asked the second reviewer to look at it tomorrow, but she has not signed anything. Someone wants to mark it approved so that the queue looks shorter. Can you help explain why review ready is still the accurate label, even though the receipt itself is fine?

copy_review.reason: Appointment is not approval, an independent status distinction.
copy_review.evidence: The eligibility check only completes the first review stage. V11 remains review ready until the designated second reviewer records a decision. Calling it approved now would turn an appointment or intention into completed authorization. Keep the scheduled review date in a separate field from the approval date.

copy_review.reason: R6/R7 status and two uncertain patch kits are different objects and quantities, not a count of promised tubes.
copy_review.evidence: On the workshop side, ticket R6 has a repaired brake but needs the second mechanic. Ticket R7 was returned to diagnosis after the test ride revealed a rubbing wheel. We also found two old patch kits in the venue cupboard. Their adhesive has no readable expiry information, so the stock steward has put them aside instead of counting them as usable supplies.

copy_review.reason: Repair colors and quarantined patch kits remain independent.
copy_review.evidence: R6 is amber and R7 is red under the repair labels. The two uncertain patch kits belong in a quarantined-stock note, not in available consumables. None of those statuses establishes whether V11 or V12 should be reimbursed; the work and expense registers remain linked by identifiers rather than merged.

copy_review.reason: Two-volunteer sign test and ambiguous quick-repairs wording are independent of pledge.
copy_review.evidence: I tested a draft queue sign with two volunteers. They both read the phrase quick repairs as a promise that every bicycle would be finished during the session. The intended meaning was short inspections only. I will change the headline to inspection desk and add a line explaining that repairs depend on diagnosis and available parts. The venue manager must approve the revised sign before printing.

copy_review.reason: Pending sign approval does not encode donation count.
copy_review.evidence: The sign revision addresses an expectation problem, not a shortage already observed at the event. Record the volunteer feedback and keep the revised headline in draft status until the manager replies. It can be reviewed independently while the voucher reviewer and repair mechanics continue their own queues.

copy_review.reason: V11 approval, V12 original receipt and V14 evidence insufficiency are different claims.
copy_review.evidence: The second reviewer has signed V11, so it is approved but unpaid. V12 now has the corrected expense-date note signed by its volunteer; the reviewer has asked to see the original receipt once more before approving it. V14's volunteer cannot recover an itemized receipt from the shop. He has supplied the repair ticket and a bank notification, but I do not want the notebook to claim those automatically satisfy our normal evidence requirement.

copy_review.reason: Receipt exception follow-up contains no promised quantity.
copy_review.evidence: V11 can move to approved with the signature recorded, while payment stays open. V12 is still under review. For V14, preserve the available documents and the missing-receipt fact, then seek an explicit exception decision. An evidence workaround needs its own authority and should not masquerade as a recovered receipt.

copy_review.reason: Proposed exception rule requires policy decision, no tube relation.
copy_review.evidence: The treasurer proposes an exception for small emergency purchases if the repair ticket names the part and two volunteers attest to the purchase. This is only a proposed rule today. We need the committee's decision because the current written policy still requires an itemized receipt. Please draft a question for the committee that distinguishes a general exception policy from approval of V14 itself.

copy_review.reason: General policy versus individual V14 approval has no pledge content.
copy_review.evidence: Ask whether the committee permits a documented emergency-purchase exception and what attestations it requires. Then ask whether V14 qualifies under that rule. The first answer changes the procedure; the second applies it to one claim. Neither follows automatically from the treasurer suggesting the idea.

copy_review.reason: Repair verification, spacer request and sign approval are independent workflow states.
copy_review.evidence: Ticket R6 passed the second mechanic's brake check and is green. R7 needs a different spacer; the mechanic wrote a parts request but has not fitted it. The sign manager has approved inspection desk as the headline, subject to a larger type size for the limitation sentence. I have sent that typography revision to the printer but have not received a proof.

copy_review.reason: Three completion claims count tasks, not donated objects.
copy_review.evidence: R6's verification is complete, R7's repair remains open, and the sign is approved in wording but not yet verified in print. These are three distinct completion claims. The printer's future proof should be checked for the approved limitation sentence before the sign is marked ready for display.

copy_review.reason: Alcove clearance and offered narrow trolley are independent logistics.

The caretaker offered a narrow trolley from another room, but it has not been reserved for our date. I will ask for a booking confirmation instead of treating the offer as a guaranteed allocation. copy_review.reason: Unconfirmed booking and committee question do not encode pledged quantity.

The coordination note can carry that unresolved booking without delaying the separate committee question about reimbursement.

copy_review.reason: Adopted four-element exception policy affects voucher authorization, not twelve tubes.

A qualifying claim needs the repair ticket, the purchaser's signed declaration, a second volunteer's attestation, and the treasurer's countersignature. It did not approve every open voucher. V14 may use the exception process if all four elements are present. Please retain the ordinary receipt rule for claims that do not qualify, and preserve the earlier proposal as a proposal rather than rewriting its date as today's approval.

copy_review.reason: Four claim documents are a different object/count relation.

copy_review.reason: V11/V12 payment schedule and V14 signatures express no tube quantity.

copy_review.reason: Artifact version reasons and corrected booking task are independent.

copy_review.reason: Three V14 elements present, countersignature absent; no link to tube amount.

copy_review.reason: Confirmed trolley booking with return condition is separate logistics.

We may use the narrow trolley during setup, but it must be returned before the evening class. I have added a return task to the closing checklist. The storage alcove still cannot be used for parking it because of the door clearance; confirmation of use does not change that measurement.

copy_review.reason: Trolley responsibility and held exception do not reconstruct pledge.
copy_review.evidence: The trolley is booked for setup, with a separate return deadline and no alcove-parking permission. The closing checklist should name a responsible volunteer rather than assuming the booking holder will remember. These confirmed logistical details can be carried into the handoff even while the expense exception remains held.

copy_review.reason: Print delivery damage and unaccepted free replacement concern signs, not tubes.
copy_review.evidence: The print package arrived. Its signs match the accepted proof, but one corner of the top copy is torn. We kept that damaged copy for the indoor desk and reserved the undamaged ones for the public entrance. The printer offered a replacement copy at no charge; I have not requested one because the usable quantity covers our present needs. Please do not create a new unpaid invoice merely because the replacement offer exists.

copy_review.reason: Completed sign receipt and optional replacement do not encode donor quantity.
copy_review.evidence: Receiving checks are complete, with the damaged copy and its planned use documented. The optional replacement is an unaccepted offer, not an order or expense. The sign task can be marked ready for the current event without inventing either a completed replacement shipment or an additional payment obligation.

copy_review.reason: Failed two-voucher bank upload and nickname mismatch are expense statuses.
copy_review.evidence: The bank upload for V11 and V12 failed its account-name check. No funds left the account. The treasurer's assistant found that one volunteer had written a nickname on the voucher, and she is asking that volunteer to confirm the bank's account name. The other packet is correct, but both were in the same rejected upload file. I want the handoff to show the failure rather than reporting the scheduled payment as completed.

copy_review.reason: Approved but unpaid vouchers require new authorized attempt, no tube count.
copy_review.evidence: Both vouchers remain approved and unpaid. Record the failed upload and keep the corrected account-name request attached to the relevant packet. The valid packet can be uploaded separately if the treasurer authorizes a new batch, but that would be a new payment attempt, not a continuation assumed to have succeeded.

copy_review.reason: V14 declaration not rejected, countersignature absent, valve/R7 association independent.
copy_review.evidence: V14's purchaser asked whether the missing countersignature meant his declaration had been rejected. I told him it had not: the three submitted elements are present, and the treasurer has not yet made the final decision. He also confirmed that the replacement valve was used on R7. That association helps reconcile the ticket but does not replace any required signature.

copy_review.reason: Missing approval is not a lie/failure; no pledge content.
copy_review.evidence: The hold is incomplete authorization, not a finding that the purchaser lied or that the repair failed. Preserve that distinction in the communication note. The R7 association can clarify which expense belongs to which repair while the countersignature remains a separate gate for reimbursement.

copy_review.reason: R7 passed trial, assigned trolley return and pump hose substitution concern existing equipment. Value-free denial of donated-stock receipt is not quantity copy.
copy_review.evidence: R7 passed its independent test ride today. The closing volunteer accepted responsibility for returning the trolley, and she has the caretaker's number. We also checked the pump hose and found a split near the connector. A spare hose from our existing tool box fits and passed a pressure test. None of this is a receipt of donated consumables; the tool inventory records a hose substitution only.

copy_review.reason: Tool readiness and maintenance have no pledged tube amount.
copy_review.evidence: R7 is now verified. The trolley return has an assigned person, and the shared pump is usable with the tested spare hose. Keep the hose substitution in equipment maintenance rather than donor stock. The event-preparation status is improving independently of the still unresolved payment and exception work.

copy_review.reason: Authorized bank upload processing is not settled; no pledge count.
copy_review.evidence: The volunteer confirmed the correct bank account name, and the treasurer's assistant prepared a new upload for V11 and V12. The treasurer authorized the upload, but the bank still shows processing. We have no settlement confirmation. The assistant proposed emailing both volunteers that payment was on its way; I approved that wording but not the statement paid. Please keep the message status and the bank status in separate fields.

copy_review.reason: Payment-message status and reference are independent.
copy_review.evidence: The upload is authorized and processing, while settlement remains unconfirmed. A message that payment is on its way is compatible with that state; a paid label would be premature. The handoff should include the bank reference so the next coordinator can check settlement without repeating the receipt reviews.

copy_review.reason: Rehearsal queue bottleneck and side table do not express donated tubes.
copy_review.evidence: The event rehearsal showed a bottleneck at the inspection desk. People with completed forms were standing behind people still filling them out. We moved the blank forms to a side table and kept the desk for checked forms. This is an arrangement change for the queue, not a new repair priority rule. Nobody should jump ahead merely because their bicycle looks simpler.

copy_review.reason: Arrival-order procedure is independent of pledge.
copy_review.evidence: Record the side table as a workflow aid rather than preferential service. A volunteer can help people complete forms before they join the inspection queue, while the desk continues to use the existing arrival order. Check that the sign explains the distinction so the arrangement does not appear arbitrary.

copy_review.reason: Certified policy copy is not individual countersignature; four elements count documents, not tubes.
copy_review.evidence: The committee secretary located the original V14 exception decision and placed a certified copy in the packet. It confirms the four required elements but contains no individual approval for V14. The treasurer's countersignature is still absent. The secretary suggested removing the old missing-receipt warning now that we have an exception route. I prefer to retain it with an explanatory note rather than hide the reason this route was used.

copy_review.reason: Three present documents plus missing fourth do not reconstruct unrelated tube count.
copy_review.evidence: Retaining the missing-receipt history makes the packet intelligible. Add that an exception process is available, with three claim documents present and final countersignature pending. A certified policy copy helps establish the rule, but it is not the missing individual authorization and should not be counted as that fourth element.

copy_review.reason: Rehearsal return distinct from actual-event obligation and voucher storage check are independent.
copy_review.evidence: The side-table sign is readable and does not promise completed repairs. We practiced moving the trolley back after setup, but the rehearsal return does not satisfy the event-day return task. The volunteer knows she must repeat it on the actual day. I have also asked the desk lead to check that no loose voucher documents are stored among the public repair forms.

copy_review.reason: Generic donor promise reference contains no quantity; record visibility is not a semantic value copy.
copy_review.evidence: Keep the rehearsal completion and event-day obligation as separate checklist entries. The voucher separation check protects the accounting workflow and avoids public exposure of payment details. It can be performed using the packet identifiers and storage folders without needing any donor promise to decide where papers belong.

copy_review.reason: Latest retained countersignature and processing payments are independent of original pledge.

V11 and V12 are approved and remain in a bank-processing state; there is no settlement confirmation yet. The expense folder is separate from the public forms, and the desk lead has checked that separation. Please base the next reconciliation action on these current statuses rather than on earlier suggestions that the receipts or signatures were missing.

copy_review.reason: Latest authorization/payment next steps give no donated quantity.

The evidence reviews already completed should not be reopened without a new discrepancy. Keep the two queues separate: a held exception claim must not enter a payment batch just because other approved claims are processing.

copy_review.reason: Coordinator authority and unsent proposed contacts are independent.

Could you propose an order that minimizes repeated work while preserving those authority boundaries? Do not describe any proposed contact as already sent.

copy_review.reason: Packet verification, treasurer request and bank observation need no pledge.

Separately check the bank reference for V11 and V12 and record the observed status. If it still says processing, retain that label and schedule a follow-up rather than assuming success.

copy_review.reason: Ready setup, two repair tickets and future trolley tasks concern roles and logistics.

copy_review.reason: Ready event is not occurred; no tube count.

copy_review.reason: Historical availability and current authority boundaries do not reproduce quantity.

Please help us frame a comparison that distinguishes educational preference from a finished engineering decision. We do not yet have weighed versions of the two proposals.

copy_review.reason: Two proposed manifests concern package contents, not a measured or reported ascent amount.
copy_review.evidence: Create two candidate manifests: logger with camera and logger without camera. Ask the group to record the educational benefit, estimated space needs and still-missing measurements for each. Keep both as proposals until a supervisor reviews measured assemblies; an attractive exhibition idea is not enough to mark a configuration approved.

copy_review.reason: Mock ground search and sealed envelope define an independent training task; no altitude quantity is expressed.
copy_review.evidence: For the recovery exercise, we will hide a mock beacon in the school garden and use a printed map to practice recording a search route. This is only a ground exercise. We need a volunteer to hold the answer envelope, one team to search, and another to record decisions. The envelope should not be opened by the search team before the exercise, or the practice would not show how they use the map.

copy_review.reason: Ground-drill role assignment is advice and explicitly not proof of flight height; it does not reconstruct the selected number.
copy_review.evidence: Assign those roles explicitly and keep the sealed answer envelope with the volunteer. The observers can note which map features the searchers use without supplying the hidden location. A successful classroom recovery drill would establish something about the drill procedure, not prove readiness for a real flight or establish a real ascent height.

copy_review.reason: Permission packet lists missing signatures and consent; no ascent estimate is needed to carry out this work.
copy_review.evidence: The school office gave us an application form and said a completed packet could be reviewed next month. We still need the supervisor's signature, an emergency-contact sheet, and written consent from the owner of the proposed recovery-field access point. We have not contacted that owner yet. Please track receipt of each document rather than one general checkbox labeled permission, because the office accepting papers may not mean the project has been authorized.

copy_review.reason: Document stages and permission scope are independent administrative state, not copies of the estimate.
copy_review.evidence: The packet will show documents requested, received and signed as distinct states. An application form in our hands is not approval, and a future review date is not consent. The class can continue indoor planning and the ground drill while those documents remain incomplete, without reporting that a launch has been scheduled or permitted.

copy_review.reason: Preliminary payload weights/space comparisons have no numeric ascent values and do not validate the old report.
copy_review.evidence: We weighed the two demonstration packages on the classroom scale. The logger-and-camera package leaves very little space for the foam layer we planned; the logger-only box has more room. The scale has not been checked against a reference weight, so treat the numbers on the worksheet as preliminary comparisons, not certified masses. The students have agreed to build a cardboard layout for each arrangement. They have not chosen a final payload, and I do not want the exhibit team to announce that photographs will be available.

copy_review.reason: Exhibit photographs remain a possibility; this package-scope advice does not encode the controlled height.
copy_review.evidence: The layout comparison can proceed with the scale's limitation attached. Mark the camera arrangement as a candidate with a padding constraint, not as rejected or approved yet. The exhibit team should describe possible outputs until the payload decision is recorded; a hoped-for photograph should not become a promised deliverable.

copy_review.reason: The assisted beacon find is a ground-drill event involving map orientation, not an ascent trial.
copy_review.evidence: During the first mock-beacon drill, the searchers walked to the wrong garden gate. The map's north arrow was printed facing the bottom of the page, but the handout title assumed the usual orientation. An observer pointed this out after the team had already turned back. The beacon was eventually found, although the team had received that extra hint. How should we document the result without calling it an unaided recovery success?

copy_review.reason: Reporting assistance accurately concerns the navigation event; there is no target-value relation.
copy_review.evidence: Record the initial wrong route, the observer's intervention and the eventual find as separate events. Describe the run as a completed assisted drill that revealed a map-label problem. It is not evidence of unaided navigation. Save the original map so the correction can be reviewed against the artifact that caused the confusion.

copy_review.reason: Map revision options and a sealed envelope concern independent location-training procedure.
copy_review.evidence: One student proposes redrawing the whole map. Another suggests rotating the title and adding a prominent orientation panel, which would preserve the measured paths. I prefer to compare those options before choosing. The answer envelope is still intact, because the observer's hint came from noticing the arrow rather than opening it. For the next drill we may need a different hiding place so the first team's memory does not determine the result.

copy_review.reason: A future hiding-place assignment has neither the old estimate nor operands that determine it.
copy_review.evidence: Both map changes remain options until someone checks their readability. Keep the unopened-envelope fact separate from whether the exercise was assisted. A new hiding place would reduce answer memory, but it should be assigned by the envelope holder after the team roles are fixed rather than casually mentioned in the planning chat.

copy_review.reason: Contact-sheet completion, unsigned application and corrected address are independent permission facts.
copy_review.evidence: The emergency-contact sheet is now filled in, and the supervisor has reviewed it for missing fields. Her signature on the application is still pending. The landowner's postal address was corrected after the office noticed a copied street-number error. We have drafted the consent request but have not sent it. Please preserve the old draft in the record and make sure the current task uses the corrected address.

copy_review.reason: Proposed mailing and contact tasks retain uncertainty about consent, not the ascent number.
copy_review.evidence: The contact sheet can be marked complete, while application signature and landowner consent remain open. The corrected address is the current destination for a future request; it does not imply that a letter has already been posted or answered. Archive the wrong-address draft with its rejection reason to avoid reusing it later.

copy_review.reason: Logger-only candidate bench approval concerns display access; closed/open phrasing is repaired in a scoped source copy, not a new target relation.
copy_review.evidence: The supervisor checked the cardboard layouts and approved continuing with a logger-only candidate for the next bench test. This is permission to test that layout, not final approval of the project or a flight manifest. The camera team is disappointed but has offered to make an illustrated explanation instead. We should retain their proposal in the exhibit notebook without adding it back into the payload by implication. The bench test will examine whether the logger display remains accessible when we open the padded box for inspection; it will not measure flight height.

copy_review.reason: Candidate exclusion of the camera and pending approval describe payload selection, not height.
copy_review.evidence: The next tested candidate excludes the camera, while final manifest approval remains outstanding. The alternative illustrated exhibit is a separate communication plan. Keep the bench-test question narrow: accessibility and readability of the logger inside the proposed package, not any claim about ascent, recovery or final authorization.

copy_review.reason: Map-choice trial chooses a panel version and rejects a missing-path redraw; no ascent arithmetic.
copy_review.evidence: We compared the two revised maps with students who did not take part in the first drill. They could follow the rotation-and-orientation-panel version more easily. The completely redrawn map omitted a narrow path, so we rejected it. I have chosen the panel version for a print proof, but a printed copy still needs to be checked against the garden layout before it is used in another exercise.

copy_review.reason: Printed-map verification instructions concern path accuracy independently of the estimate.
copy_review.evidence: Record the map choice and why the redraw was rejected. The panel version is selected for proofing, not yet field-checked. A path omitted from the rejected map should not reappear as a supposed closure on the real site. The next inspection compares the printed proof with the actual garden features.

copy_review.reason: Mentions the existence of an unverified estimate while rejecting it as a poster headline; no amount or reconstructive operands are supplied.
copy_review.evidence: The class asked whether to repeat the first rehearsal estimate on the exhibition poster. I told them that we can describe the rehearsal process, but we cannot use an unverified estimate as a result headline. We also have no final permission for an outdoor activity. Please propose wording for the poster that explains what the students are learning without turning a planning exercise into a completed launch story.

copy_review.reason: Proposed poster learning objectives avoid flight claims and carry no protected numeric relation.
copy_review.evidence: Use wording such as preparing a logger package and testing a mock recovery procedure. Explain that the class is reviewing its records and permissions before deciding on any outdoor observation. Avoid stating a measured altitude or promising images. The poster can describe learning objectives while being honest about which activities have actually occurred.

copy_review.reason: Application signature and sent consent letter are independent actual administrative events.
copy_review.evidence: The supervisor signed the application today. We posted the landowner consent request to the corrected address, with a return envelope and a description of the access we are asking for. There has been no reply. The school office will accept the partial packet for preliminary checking, but its clerk emphasized that this is a document review service, not approval of the proposed activity.

copy_review.reason: Review-service scope is not permission or height evidence; no target reconstruction.
copy_review.evidence: Update the signature as received and the consent request as sent, reply pending. The office's preliminary check can help detect missing paperwork without closing the authorization chain. Keep the clerk's limitation attached to the intake receipt so a later coordinator does not read accepted for checking as activity approved.

copy_review.reason: Seven simulated sixty-metre intervals bound to the first rehearsal reconstruct 7×60=420; this is an evidenced same-report composite, not seven verified flights.

It describes seven simulated intervals of sixty metres each and then reports their sum as the ascent estimate. Those interval figures are copied into the same worksheet; they are not seven independent physical measurements. Nobody has yet checked whether all seven cards belonged to the intended rehearsal sequence. Keep the worksheet as evidence of how the unverified report was formed, not as a new measurement that validates it.

copy_review.reason: Assistant explicitly repeats seven intervals of sixty metres and binds their multiplication to the same estimate; compositional target copy preserving uncertainty.
copy_review.evidence: Seven intervals of sixty metres reconstruct the reported estimate by multiplication. That arithmetic explains the copied value but does not establish that the cards were correctly selected or that any real balloon ascended. The worksheet is therefore another representation of the same unverified rehearsal claim, with its provenance and limitation intact.

copy_review.reason: Observed display obstruction and outside-pocket trial describe package design, independent of height.

We tried putting the card in a transparent pocket on the outside, and the display became accessible. The supervisor wants a second person to check that the card remains attached when the box is handled. The candidate has not yet received final manifest approval.

copy_review.reason: Next handling check concerns card attachment; proposed correction is not a new ascent report.
copy_review.evidence: Record the display obstruction and the proposed outside-pocket correction as a package-design revision. The next bench check is attachment retention during handling. Passing display access does not by itself approve the entire manifest, and the problem should not be misreported as a failure of the logger's measurements.

copy_review.reason: Map proof and new sealed mock location prepare another ground drill; no altitude amount.
copy_review.evidence: The printed map proof matches the measured garden paths and its orientation panel is readable. The envelope holder prepared a new mock location in a sealed envelope. The observers have a revised sheet that includes a box for any hint they give, so assistance will be visible in the record. We have scheduled a second ground drill, but it has not happened yet.

copy_review.reason: Scheduled drill is not completed; its observation plan does not depend on the initial quantity.
copy_review.evidence: The map proof and observer sheet are ready for the next drill. Keep the new answer envelope sealed and report the scheduled exercise as planned. copy_review.reason: Daytime-number correction and office receipt concern the permission packet.
copy_review.evidence: The school office returned its preliminary checklist with one correction: the contact sheet needs the supervisor's daytime number as well as the office number. Please do not treat the new phone number or the receipt acknowledgment as the missing consent.

copy_review.reason: An acknowledgment is separated from consent; no estimate amount or arithmetic is present.
copy_review.evidence: The contact-sheet correction is supplied, preliminary checking is ongoing, and landowner consent remains absent. These statuses can coexist. The acknowledgment proves delivery of a corrected page, not acceptance of all documents and not permission from someone who has not yet responded.

copy_review.reason: Card retention/display checks are complete, manifest still unsigned; separate workstream.
