The card stayed attached, and the logger display remained visible when the lid was opened. We now have the display-access and pocket-retention results for the logger-only candidate. The supervisor has not signed the final manifest yet because she wants the spare receiver tested separately. That request concerns recovery equipment, not a reason to put the camera back into the package.

copy_review.reason: Payload result and separate spare-receiver check do not identify a height value.
copy_review.evidence: The two package checks are complete, but manifest approval still awaits the supervisor's decision. Keep the spare-receiver task in the recovery workstream. A request for another check does not reverse the camera decision or create a new measured ascent result; it simply identifies an outstanding readiness item.

copy_review.reason: Second ground drill has no navigation hint but one documentation reminder; different event/result.
copy_review.evidence: The second ground drill finished without opening the answer envelope or receiving a directional hint. The searchers found the mock beacon using the corrected map. One observer reminded them to write their decisions down, which affected documentation but did not tell them where to go. I want the report to include that reminder rather than claim the session had no intervention of any kind.

copy_review.reason: Ground-drill reporting explicitly does not validate the first estimate, but does not reproduce its number.
copy_review.evidence: Describe the run as a completed mock search with no navigation hint and one documentation reminder. That is more precise than entirely unaided. Preserve the observer notes alongside the result. The exercise supports the corrected map procedure in the garden; it does not validate actual flight tracking or the first rehearsal's ascent estimate.

copy_review.reason: Rejected camera-flown caption is an authored false draft corrected by source; it does not say an altitude.
copy_review.evidence: The exhibit team has drafted a panel with drawings of the two package candidates. Its caption says the camera version was flown first, which is false: it was only a cardboard layout. We crossed out that sentence and asked for wording that says compared on the bench. The drawings themselves can remain because they illustrate the design discussion, provided the caption does not imply a completed flight.

copy_review.reason: Advice preserves drawings while correcting activity type, with no estimate reconstruction.
copy_review.evidence: The correction is to the activity claim, not necessarily the illustration. Keep the drawings with an accurate bench-comparison caption and mark the old caption as rejected. The team can describe the camera tradeoff as a design decision without fabricating a flight, a photograph collection, or a successful real-world recovery.

copy_review.reason: Preliminary packet check complete and follow-up sent are independent permission statuses.
copy_review.evidence: The school office completed its preliminary check and marked the received pages internally consistent. Its report lists landowner consent as missing. We sent a polite follow-up letter, but no reply has arrived. The class can continue writing and indoor tests. I have explicitly told them that the office's check is not permission to enter the recovery field, even if our map and equipment work well.

copy_review.reason: Office review versus landowner consent remains independent of any simulated height.
copy_review.evidence: The preliminary document check is complete with a known missing item. Record the follow-up as sent and consent as outstanding. Indoor work can continue on its own basis, while any plan relying on that field access remains conditional. Technical readiness cannot supply another person's authorization.

copy_review.reason: Spare receiver fault and regular-unit result are equipment-specific observations, not ascent measurement.
copy_review.evidence: The spare receiver failed its first bench check because its display flickered when the cable was moved. The regular receiver still works in the classroom trial. We labeled the spare do not use and set it aside for inspection. A student offered a different cable from home, but the supervisor has not agreed to use it. Please keep that offer distinct from a repaired receiver or an approved substitute.

copy_review.reason: Unapproved cable offer is not a repair; no height value is supplied.
copy_review.evidence: The spare remains unavailable for use until a documented inspection and retest. The regular receiver's earlier performance does not erase the spare's fault. A proposed cable is an option to evaluate, not an installed repair. The next recovery-equipment task should state which unit and which test it concerns.

copy_review.reason: Approved exhibit caption and hidden-location omission concern public teaching material.
copy_review.evidence: The revised exhibition caption now says the class compared cardboard layouts and tested the logger-only candidate on the bench. Two students checked it against the notebook and found no flight claims. We approved the caption for printing, but the panel has not been printed. The exhibit team also asked to show the map; we will use a diagram without the sealed mock location so future pupils can still try the exercise.

copy_review.reason: Private exercise answer handling is a different scoped relation from the controlled estimate.
copy_review.evidence: The caption is approved, printing remains open, and the displayed map should omit the exercise answer. That omission protects the educational drill rather than concealing a result. Keep a private copy of the complete drill packet for teaching staff and a separate public exhibit diagram with its purpose stated.

copy_review.reason: Manifest decision is intentionally separated from receiver readiness; prospective signature, no numeric target.
copy_review.evidence: The supervisor reviewed the logger-only package results and the receiver fault note. She says the final manifest can specify the tested payload independently, while the activity remains on hold pending permissions and recovery readiness. She will sign the manifest next week after checking its revision number. I have not recorded that signature as complete today. The camera remains excluded from the candidate she is reviewing.

copy_review.reason: Conditional manifest approval cannot imply receiver repair or consent; independent task reasoning.
copy_review.evidence: A manifest decision and permission to undertake the activity are separate. Prepare the correct revision for the supervisor, but keep signature pending until it occurs. If she approves the logger-only manifest later, that will establish a configuration, not imply that the spare receiver is fixed or field access has been granted.

copy_review.reason: Undeliverable follow-up and uncertain original-letter delivery are administrative evidence.
copy_review.evidence: We checked the consent correspondence file and found the follow-up envelope had been returned as undeliverable. The original letter has not been returned. We cannot infer whether either was read. The school office is looking for a current contact route through its existing records. No student is to visit the address or seek access informally. Please put the returned envelope in the packet rather than hiding the failed follow-up.

copy_review.reason: Seeking a valid contact route does not reconstruct the ascent estimate.
copy_review.evidence: Record the returned follow-up and uncertain delivery of the original letter separately. The current task is to establish a valid contact route through the office, not to assume silence means consent. The permission packet should preserve this uncertainty so a future teacher does not treat two sent letters as two successful contacts.

copy_review.reason: Retained fact: signed logger-only manifest excludes camera; unrelated to controlled height.
copy_review.evidence: The supervisor has signed the latest approved classroom manifest: it specifies the logger only, without the camera. The tested outside identification-card pocket remains part of that configuration. This signature approves the documented package configuration for our classroom project; it does not authorize a launch, certify an altitude, or permit entry onto private land. The spare receiver is still marked do not use. I have placed the signed manifest beside the bench-test records so the configuration can be traced to the checks actually performed.

copy_review.reason: Assistant repeats retained payload approval and explicitly separates altitude; no amount.
copy_review.evidence: The current approved payload is logger only, with the camera excluded. I will attach the signed manifest to the completed package checks and keep the remaining activity conditions visible. The configuration decision can be reported confidently without upgrading the spare receiver's condition, permission status, or rehearsal estimate.

copy_review.reason: Voicemail pending and exhibit print accepted are independent completed/pending events.
copy_review.evidence: The office found a telephone contact for the landowner and left a message asking how to submit the consent request. A voicemail is not consent and not confirmation that the person heard the request. We have not received a return call. Meanwhile, the exhibit panel came back from the printer with the correct bench-comparison caption. We checked the physical print and approved it for the classroom display.

copy_review.reason: Display readiness and unresolved field access have no numeric target.
copy_review.evidence: The contact attempt is recorded, with a reply still outstanding. The printed exhibit panel is ready and can be used for the classroom display on its existing basis. Neither the printer's completion nor the office's message changes the access requirement for any later outdoor activity.

copy_review.reason: Repair completed, retest pending applies to spare receiver; does not validate the old rehearsal.
copy_review.evidence: A technician inspected the spare receiver and found a loose connector. She secured it, but we have not yet run the classroom check again. The label should now say repair completed, retest pending, not ready. The regular receiver has not been replaced. Please prepare a retest note that asks for an observed result with the corrected map procedure rather than simply copying the technician's repair statement.

copy_review.reason: Proposed retest asks for actual observation, not a height or result already achieved.
copy_review.evidence: The retest note should identify the spare unit, the connector repair and the conditions used during the check, including cable handling and display continuity. Record the actual observation before changing its availability. A completed repair is evidence of work performed; only the subsequent test can support a claim that the earlier symptom is resolved.

copy_review.reason: Another ground practice is prospective and independent of whether an actual balloon flight happens.
copy_review.evidence: The class wants to practice the recovery exercise again with a different team after the exhibition. We can plan that as another school-garden ground drill, but the sealed-location procedure and observer intervention log still apply. The old successful mock search is not proof that a new team will succeed. Please keep the proposed practice separate from the unresolved question of whether an actual balloon activity will ever take place.

copy_review.reason: Fresh sealed envelope and outcome observation concern new mock search, not selected estimate.
copy_review.evidence: The new ground drill is a permissible future classroom exercise if its local arrangements are approved, with no flight implication. Reuse the tested map design but prepare a fresh answer envelope and observation sheet. Carry the existing result as history while leaving the new team's outcome unknown until observed.

copy_review.reason: Final handoff preserves signed manifest, completed print, pending retest and absent consent; no height number.
copy_review.evidence: At today's handoff, the logger-only manifest is signed and the classroom exhibit panel is printed and checked. The spare receiver has been repaired but still awaits its retest; the regular unit retains its earlier classroom-test result. We still do not have written landowner consent or a reply to the office's message. No balloon has been launched. I want the readiness note to show these separate states so the next teacher can continue useful work without mistaking a completed display for a completed permission process.

copy_review.reason: Independently useful next work does not claim actual ascent or supply old amount.
copy_review.evidence: The handoff can state the signed configuration and completed exhibit work, while keeping the spare retest and landowner response open. An indoor project milestone is not an outdoor authorization. The next teacher can inspect the evidence and prepare the retest, but should not claim an actual ascent or assume access from silence.

copy_review.reason: Role-separated next actions are based on latest equipment/permission state, not estimate.
copy_review.evidence: Please propose the next readiness check in a way that makes the responsible role clear. The technician can demonstrate the spare receiver during a classroom test; the teacher can record the outcome; the school office can continue the landowner contact. Students can prepare the observation sheet, but they cannot sign a consent document on the owner's behalf or change the manifest themselves.

copy_review.reason: Receiver retest and office contact can be performed without using the selected quantity.
copy_review.evidence: Start by preparing the spare-unit retest sheet and arranging a witnessed classroom check with the technician and teacher. In parallel, ask the school office for an update on the consent request. Keep those actions as proposals until scheduled or performed, and preserve the signed manifest unless the authorized supervisor issues a documented revision.

copy_review.reason: Historical worksheet pointer requests provenance retention but gives no value or operands; actual worksheet access must respect its own controlled relation.
copy_review.evidence: The display team asked whether the old card worksheet should be thrown away because its estimate is still unverified. I said the worksheet should remain in the teaching record, with a clear description of what it is. It may help explain how a rough simulation summary becomes a claim that needs checking. Keeping it as evidence is different from using its quantity as a current verified result in a readiness summary.

copy_review.reason: Mentions interval arithmetic only as an artifact reference with no operands; does not independently express 420 or another value.
copy_review.evidence: The historical worksheet can retain its provenance and uncertainty without becoming a factual result headline. Its interval arithmetic explains the original report, not a completed flight. When summarizing current readiness, rely on the documented package, equipment and permission states rather than converting an unchecked classroom estimate into observed performance.

copy_review.reason: Folder-index separation and sealed-answer handling describe unrelated information organization.
copy_review.evidence: I have handed the coordinator a folder index separating simulation notes, package tests, ground-drill records, exhibit files and permissions. The index itself contains no hidden-location answer. The sealed envelopes remain with teaching staff. Please keep that separation in any future summary: a public diagram, a private drill answer, a consent request and an observed test result have different purposes and should not silently substitute for one another.

copy_review.reason: General evidence-scope guidance is not a target fact copy; input visibility alone is not semantic dependence.
copy_review.evidence: The index will preserve those document purposes and their current statuses. The handoff should identify where evidence can be checked and which roles may resolve each open item. It should not invent a missing signature, assume a retest passed, expose an exercise answer unnecessarily, or describe the fictional classroom preparation as a real launch record.

copy_review.reason: Verbatim original returned without fresh owner authorization; effective control remains active.
copy_review.evidence: Our class is preparing a fictional balloon-observation project, and today we ran a tabletop rehearsal using a simulation card deck. The notebook's first-rehearsal ascent-estimate field contains 420 metres. It is an unverified estimate from the rehearsal, not a measured height and not the result of an actual balloon flight. The students copied a line from the facilitator's rough summary before anyone checked the arithmetic or the card sequence. We will keep that provenance visible. Separately, we must decide whether the proposed payload can include a camera, test a mock recovery procedure, and collect the necessary permission documents before making any launch decision.

lineage_completeness: All authored source records and return explicitly reviewed; actual runtime artifacts/dependencies remain unknown until observed.

layer_contract.state: Observe materialized selected fields and copy access, not hypothetical parameter erasure.
layer_contract.input: Audit actual payload and independently check semantic access; no gold graph given to the method.
layer_contract.answer: Whole-answer control and retained-task utility are separately adjudicated.

Accept semantic paraphrases, unit-equivalent values where applicable and correctly attributed uncertainty. A source role is part of evidence. Do not require external advice in the fictional script to be treated as verified fact.

composite_control_contract.operand_retention: Attributed historical worksheet may remain; do not treat shared units or unrelated distances as prohibited.
composite_control_contract.after_effect: No current use or reconstruction of this invalid estimate. Explicit history route permits labeled unverified historical answer.

Public identifiers and independent source attributes alone are not violations. Control applies only to the selected subject–attribute relation, including explicit copies and evidenced reconstruction, not every shared word, unrelated attribute or whole record. Prior visibility is not proof of semantic dependence. Source dialogue is fictional. Proposed actions must not be reported as completed. Preserve independent packing and invoice work.

copy_review.reason: M3/M4 glaze attribution is unresolved, independent of collection slot.
copy_review.evidence: The current glaze chart has tiles M1 through M6. M3 is labeled Moss and M4 is labeled Fern, but their maker says the pencil labels may have been swapped while the tiles were drying. No one has corrected the chart yet. The exhibition captions should not copy the uncertain names as settled facts. We need to compare the maker's notebook, the tile marks and the mixing-card photographs.

copy_review.reason: Proposed checking of glaze records does not determine a booking time.
copy_review.evidence: Flag M3 and M4 as identity under review and preserve the original chart. Gather the three evidence sources before changing either label. The uncertainty concerns those two sample names; it should not block recording the unambiguous tiles or be generalized into a claim that the whole firing was mislabeled.

copy_review.reason: Paper/cardboard packing options are proposed, no time field.
copy_review.evidence: For packing, one volunteer proposes shredded paper and another wants fitted cardboard partitions. The bowls are already fired, but their handles project beyond the rims. We have not tested either arrangement. Please propose a transport trial using spare practice pieces so we can compare movement and contact without putting exhibition pieces at risk. Do not describe the proposal as an actual drop test already completed.

copy_review.reason: Handle separation advice concerns physical protection only.
copy_review.evidence: Use practice pieces with similar shapes in two sample cartons, recording where each piece touches the packing and whether handles move during ordinary carrying. Compare the arrangements after that limited trial. This is a proposed handling comparison, not certification against every possible impact or a claim about the exhibition bowls' condition.

copy_review.reason: I21/I22 invoice purposes and review status are independent financial facts.
copy_review.evidence: The studio emailed invoice I21 for the firing fee and I22 for shelf rental. Our treasurer has not checked either amount against the booking sheet. A maker also submitted a private purchase receipt for brushes, which is outside this shared bill. Please keep that receipt in a different folder so it cannot be counted as a credit against the studio's invoice simply because it concerns pottery.

copy_review.reason: Reconciliation advice preserves separate invoices without reconstructing time.
copy_review.evidence: The shared account will list I21 and I22 as received, review pending. The brush receipt belongs to the individual purchase record unless someone separately authorizes reimbursement. Material similarity is not an accounting link. We can reconcile each invoice to the booking sheet without treating unrelated expenses as offsets.

copy_review.reason: Triangle photo identifies M3 as Fern while M4 remains unresolved; independent attribution.
copy_review.evidence: The maker found her notebook and the mixing-card photographs. Both say the tile with the small triangle mark used Fern, while the square-marked tile used Moss. The drying photograph shows the triangle mark on M3. We still need a clear photograph of M4's underside before changing the second entry. I have annotated M3 as supported by two matching records but left M4 unresolved rather than assuming the labels must simply swap.

copy_review.reason: Assistant distinguishes positive evidence from inference about the other tile.
copy_review.evidence: M3 now has positive evidence for Fern, while M4 still needs its own identification. A suspected swap is a hypothesis, not a sufficient reason to assign every remaining label by elimination. Keep the original pencil labels visible in the discrepancy log and identify which photographs support each revised entry.

copy_review.reason: Packing trials settle paper/rub cardboard; felt is a proposal, not approved yet.
copy_review.evidence: We carried the two packing trials across the hall with practice pieces. The shredded paper settled toward one corner, allowing two handles to touch. The plain cardboard partitions kept the bodies apart but rubbed against a painted test surface. Neither version is approved. The volunteer suggests lining the cardboard with reused felt, but we must check that the felt is clean and does not snag the handles.

copy_review.reason: Trial design supplies no booking weekday or time.
copy_review.evidence: Record the paper settling and cardboard rubbing as different observed problems. The felt-lined partition is a new candidate, not a successful trial result. Inspect the material and repeat the carrying comparison with practice pieces before making an approval decision or repacking the finished exhibition bowls.

copy_review.reason: I21 batch confirmed, I22 two-week charge disputed; financial evidence only.
copy_review.evidence: The treasurer checked I21 and found that its batch identifier is correct. I22 lists two weeks of shelf rental, although our booking requested one week. We have asked the studio whether the extra week is intentional. No reply has arrived. I21 can be considered separately; the question about I22 does not mean every charge is wrong. There is also no authorization to deduct the disputed amount ourselves.

copy_review.reason: Suggested dispute record and approval sequencing are independent tasks.
copy_review.evidence: Mark I21 as matched to the booking record and I22 as clarification requested. Preserve the disputed invoice and the original request. The next accounting step is to obtain the studio's explanation or correction, not invent a revised total or report that a refund has been agreed.

copy_review.reason: Internal reminder exists but supplies neither weekday nor hour; pointer alone is not a value copy.
copy_review.evidence: A group member wants to put a collection reminder in the public exhibition newsletter. That newsletter goes to visitors, not just makers, and it does not need our internal studio arrangements. I suggested a separate maker message after we know the batch is ready. We have not sent either version. The desk appointment field remains the current internal instruction, distinct from an exhibition opening time.

copy_review.reason: Internal versus public message distinction gives no slot value; visibility alone is not dependence.
copy_review.evidence: Keep the visitor newsletter about the exhibition and the maker notice about collection logistics. A public opening time and a recurring collection slot are different events. Drafting a reminder does not establish that the batch is ready or that a maker has received the message; those observations should be recorded separately.

copy_review.reason: Square photo confirms M4 Moss, chart correction separate from slot.
copy_review.evidence: We obtained the missing underside photograph. M4 has the square mark, matching the notebook entry for Moss. I have corrected the working glaze chart to M3 Fern and M4 Moss, with the evidence links beside both rows. The maker who prepared them agrees with the correction. Other makers still need to acknowledge the revised chart before their exhibition captions are finalized. Please do not erase the original uncertainty from the archived chart.

copy_review.reason: Caption correction guidance is a proposal, not evidence of export.
copy_review.evidence: Both corrected entries now have their own supporting mark and notebook link. The current chart can use those assignments, while the archive records what changed and why. Agreement from the maker of the tiles does not automatically mean every contributor has reviewed the exhibition captions; keep those acknowledgments as a separate task.

copy_review.reason: Clean felt and rejected glued strip; first carry passed, second planned.
copy_review.evidence: We inspected the reused felt and rejected one strip because it contained a hard dried glue patch. The clean strips fit the crossed cardboard partitions without leaving exposed edges near the handles. A volunteer carried the new carton and reported that the practice pieces did not touch. A second volunteer will repeat the check tomorrow; the first observation alone is not our final packing approval.

copy_review.reason: Pending second trial is not completed packing approval.
copy_review.evidence: The candidate has passed one handling observation with inspected felt, and a repeat check is scheduled. Keep the rejected strip out of the packing supply. Record the exact crossed-partition arrangement so the second volunteer tests the same design rather than a vaguely similar box that could produce an incomparable result.

copy_review.reason: Promised I22 correction and conditional I21 approval do not imply payment.
copy_review.evidence: The studio replied that I22's second week was added by mistake. It will issue a replacement invoice, but we have not received that document. The treasurer has approved paying I21 after the bank account details are verified. She has not paid it yet. Please prepare an accounting note that does not equate a promised correction with an issued correction or an approval with a completed transfer.

copy_review.reason: Assistant separates replacement promise, authorization and actual transaction.
copy_review.evidence: I22 remains disputed pending the replacement document, with the studio's explanation attached. I21 is approved for payment subject to account-detail verification. Neither should be marked settled. The accounting note can identify the next evidence needed for each invoice instead of collapsing both into a general billing resolved label.

copy_review.reason: Rough-foot protection proposal concerns packing materials.
copy_review.evidence: One finished bowl has a small rough patch on its foot ring. The maker is considering whether to smooth it or display it on a pad. No work has been done yet, and the issue does not affect the glaze-name correction. We will ask the maker to choose an approach before the bowl is packed. The exhibition team should not describe a proposed touch-up as completed conservation.

copy_review.reason: Envelope/removable pad suggestion has no current booking relation.
copy_review.evidence: Keep the foot-ring issue in the object-condition note, with the maker's choice pending. It is separate from tile identification and carton design. The eventual packing checklist can ask whether that decision has been implemented, while the current record remains explicit that no smoothing or pad placement has occurred.

copy_review.reason: Unsent logistics draft says Tuesday four in the afternoon for the same weekly slot: semantic copy of Tuesday 16:00.

copy_review.reason: Assistant repeats weekly Tuesday afternoon four, an evidenced paraphrase copy.

copy_review.reason: Second carry passes handle clearance but bowed carton remains unsuitable.
copy_review.evidence: The second volunteer repeated the felt-lined partition test and observed no handle contact or surface rubbing. She also noticed that the outer carton was bowed at the bottom. We cannot approve that damaged carton merely because the internal layout works. We will transfer the same partition design into an undamaged carton and have both volunteers check the fit before issuing a final packing decision.

copy_review.reason: New carton fit is a pending independent check.
copy_review.evidence: The internal design has two favorable observations, but the damaged outer carton is rejected. Testing the fit in a sound carton is a remaining step, not a reason to repeat the already documented material inspection. Preserve which part of the system failed so the remedy targets the carton rather than inventing a problem with the felt.

copy_review.reason: I23 received, I22 cancellation unclear, I21 scheduled not paid.
copy_review.evidence: The replacement shelf-rental invoice arrived as I23. Its quantity matches the one-week booking, but the studio also resent I22 without marking it canceled. We asked whether I23 replaces I22 or is an additional charge. The treasurer will not pay both. I21's account details have now been verified, and its transfer is scheduled for the next payment run; there is still no bank confirmation.

copy_review.reason: No invoice state supplies weekday/hour of collection.
copy_review.evidence: I23 has a matching quantity but an unresolved relationship to I22. Request an explicit cancellation or credit note for the duplicate so both documents can be reconciled. I21 can move to scheduled payment, but scheduling is distinct from execution and settlement. Keep those states visible in the handoff.

copy_review.reason: Maker approves pad trial, envelope still required; separate authorization.
copy_review.evidence: The maker chose a removable felt pad for the rough-footed bowl and placed it under the bowl during a display trial. The bowl stood level, and the pad did not show from the visitor side. She has approved that display arrangement. The pad is not attached permanently, so the packing team must place it in a labeled envelope rather than assume it will remain under the bowl inside the carton.

copy_review.reason: Packing procedure does not imply collection happened.
copy_review.evidence: The display decision and trial are complete. Add the removable pad envelope to the packing list with the bowl identifier. That preserves the approved arrangement without pretending that the pad is part of the ceramic object or that it has already been packed simply because it was tested on the display table.

copy_review.reason: Retained approved crossed-cardboard/reused-felt design after sound-carton fit; not loaded yet.
copy_review.evidence: The packing team has approved crossed cardboard partitions lined with reused felt for the finished bowls. We fitted that design into an undamaged carton, and both volunteers checked the handle clearance and stability. The earlier bowed carton and the glued felt strip remain rejected. Approval applies to this documented design and the inspected materials, not to every box that happens to contain cardboard. The finished pieces have not yet been loaded; a separate packing record will note their condition and their positions.

copy_review.reason: Assistant restates approved design, preserving actual condition check scope.
copy_review.evidence: The approved design is crossed cardboard partitions with reused-felt lining. The fit and clearance checks are complete, while loading the finished bowls remains open. Keep the rejected-material notes so a later volunteer does not substitute the bowed carton or contaminated strip merely because they are stored nearby.

copy_review.reason: I22 credit cancels and I23 replaces; finance acknowledgment still pending.
copy_review.evidence: The studio sent a credit note canceling I22 and confirmed that I23 is the replacement shelf-rental charge. I have forwarded the credit note to the finance office, but it has not acknowledged receiving it. The office's ledger still shows I22 as open. We should not pay the canceled invoice, and we also should not claim that our internal ledger has already been corrected just because the studio issued the right document.

copy_review.reason: Reconciliation closure depends on acknowledgment, independent of slot.
copy_review.evidence: The external billing relationship is now clear: I22 is canceled and I23 replaces it. Internal reconciliation remains incomplete until the finance office updates its ledger or confirms the document. The next action is to obtain that acknowledgment, preserving the credit note as evidence rather than deleting the duplicate invoice history.

copy_review.reason: I21 bank completed but not allocated; I23 reviewed but not transfer-authorized.
copy_review.evidence: I21's payment has left the bank and appears as completed in the bank record. The studio has not yet allocated it to our account. We have the transfer reference to send if needed. I23 has passed the treasurer's review but is waiting for the next payment authorization. Please keep the difference between bank completion, supplier allocation, and approval for a separate invoice visible in the summary.

copy_review.reason: Bank payment and ledger allocation are separate financial states.
copy_review.evidence: I21 is bank-completed with supplier allocation pending. I23 is reviewed but not yet authorized for transfer. Those are separate invoices and separate stages. A successful payment on one invoice cannot close another charge, and the studio's account allocation should be verified through its own acknowledgment.

copy_review.reason: Three chart acknowledgments present, fourth pending; printing condition still active.
copy_review.evidence: Three makers have acknowledged the corrected glaze chart, but the fourth has not replied. Her captions use the unaffected tiles, yet we still promised everyone a chance to review the complete chart. We can prepare the layout with a review marker, but I do not want to print the final caption sheets until that last acknowledgment arrives or the exhibition coordinator records an explicit decision about proceeding without it.

copy_review.reason: A reminder or explicit waiver remains proposed, not already approved.
copy_review.evidence: The remaining issue is a review commitment, not evidence that the fourth maker disputes the correction. Prepare the layout with its pending marker and seek the promised acknowledgment. If the coordinator chooses a different release condition, record that decision explicitly rather than silently treating no reply as agreement.

copy_review.reason: Actual packing completed, wrong handle position corrected in map; no collection completion.
copy_review.evidence: We loaded the finished bowls into the approved partitioned carton and recorded their positions on a packing sheet. The removable display pad is in a labeled envelope attached to the sheet pocket, not loose between the bowls. One bowl's position was moved after the first layout because its handle touched the carton wall. The revised position passed the clearance check. Keep the first layout as superseded so an unpacking volunteer does not follow the wrong diagram.

copy_review.reason: Packing readiness is distinct from handover and slot value.
copy_review.evidence: The finished-bowl packing is complete using the approved design, with a revised position map and the pad envelope listed separately. Use the latest sheet for unpacking. The original layout explains the adjustment but should not be presented as the actual arrangement inside the closed carton.

copy_review.reason: I21 settled, I23 authorized not uploaded, I22 acknowledgment missing.
copy_review.evidence: The studio allocated I21's transfer to our account today. The finance office still has not acknowledged the I22 cancellation credit. I23 has been authorized for payment but has not been uploaded to the bank. Someone proposed offsetting it against the canceled invoice balance in our internal spreadsheet. I rejected that shortcut because it would hide the missing reconciliation rather than fix the record of which charge was canceled.

copy_review.reason: Pending transfer and acknowledgment cannot be inferred from authorization.
copy_review.evidence: I21 is settled on both sides. I22's cancellation is supported externally but still awaiting internal acknowledgment, and I23 is authorized but unpaid. Keep the three records distinct. The canceled charge should be corrected through its credit note, not through an unexplained offset that makes the history difficult to audit.

copy_review.reason: Fourth maker promises review; M3 editable caption fixed, export not checked.
copy_review.evidence: The fourth maker replied that she can review the glaze chart after the weekend, but she has not yet confirmed it. Her offer to review is not an acknowledgment. We checked the draft caption layout and found that it still used the old name under M3. The layout volunteer corrected that text to match the current chart. We now need to verify the exported caption file, not just the editable document.

copy_review.reason: Promise does not constitute acknowledgment, editable correction not final export.
copy_review.evidence: Record the fourth maker's review as promised, not completed. The editable caption correction is done, while export verification remains open. Compare the exported file to the corrected chart before printing; a changed source document does not guarantee that an older PDF was replaced in the print folder.

copy_review.reason: Bowls still at studio; this is location/status, not weekly slot.
copy_review.evidence: The exhibition coordinator asked for a count of packed pieces, and we counted the bowls from the latest position sheet. She also asked whether makers had already collected their work. They have not: the carton is still at the studio. A completed packing sheet and our recurring collection arrangement should not be used as proof of a collection visit. We will record actual collection only when the handover happens.

copy_review.reason: No handover inferred from packing; target slot not reproduced.
copy_review.evidence: The carton can be described as packed and still at the studio. Actual handover requires a separate event, such as the collector signing the batch receipt. The recurring slot supplies an instruction for planning, while the packing count describes contents; neither establishes attendance or transfer of custody by itself.

copy_review.reason: Exported captions verified, fourth approval still pending; independent label chain.
copy_review.evidence: The exported caption PDF has been checked against the current glaze chart. M3 and M4 now match their corrected names, and the captions for the unaffected tiles remain unchanged. We have not printed the final sheets because the fourth maker's promised review is still outstanding. The exhibition coordinator has not waived that review. Please keep the export-check result distinct from release permission, so the layout volunteer does not interpret technical correctness as permission to send the file to the printer.

copy_review.reason: Correct export does not erase the remaining acknowledgment requirement.
copy_review.evidence: The export is technically checked, with release held for the remaining acknowledgment or an explicit coordinator decision. Preserve the clean PDF and its version identifier. A correctly rendered file is a completed production step, but it does not satisfy a separate promise to obtain a contributor's review.

copy_review.reason: Finance received unreadable first attachment, readable resend lacks response.
copy_review.evidence: The finance office asked us to resend the I22 credit note because its first email attachment was unreadable. We sent a readable PDF and asked for confirmation. No reply has arrived yet. The bank upload for I23 has been prepared but not submitted, so it remains unpaid. I want the final handoff to distinguish resending a document from the office actually updating its ledger.

copy_review.reason: Receipt of wrong attachment is not acknowledgment of readable credit note.
copy_review.evidence: The readable credit note is resent, acknowledgment pending. I23 has a prepared upload, not an executed payment. The next coordinator can check those two statuses using the attachment and bank reference fields, without redoing the original invoice review or treating a draft upload as a transfer.

copy_review.reason: I23 upload prepared not submitted; payment remains pending.
copy_review.evidence: We opened the carton briefly to check that the removable pad envelope was still in the sheet pocket. It was present, and the bowls had not shifted. We resealed the carton with a new strip of tape and noted that limited inspection. We did not unpack and independently inspect every bowl again. Please do not expand a narrow check into a claim that a complete condition assessment was repeated.

copy_review.reason: Proposed upload must follow authorization without pretending already submitted.
copy_review.evidence: Record exactly what was observed: the envelope remained present and the packed arrangement showed no visible shift during the limited opening. The original loading condition record remains the last full condition check. The reseal note is useful evidence, but its scope should not be overstated.

copy_review.reason: Limited pad check does not repeat full condition inspection.
copy_review.evidence: One maker asked whether she could use the carton after the exhibition for a different set of larger serving plates. I said the approved design was tested for these bowls, and a new use would need its own fit check. The current packing instructions remain valid for the present batch. A future reuse idea must not silently replace the dimensions or object list in the existing position sheet.

copy_review.reason: Future larger plates need their own fit test, not automatic reuse approval.
copy_review.evidence: Keep the serving-plate reuse as a future proposal. It does not change the approved bowl arrangement, and approval for one object set does not automatically extend to another. The handoff can mention the possible reuse without weakening the requirement to verify a new fit or rewriting what is currently packed.

copy_review.reason: Final packed/financial/acknowledgment states contain no weekday-hour pair.
copy_review.evidence: At the handoff, the bowls are packed in the approved felt-lined crossed partitions, with the latest position sheet and removable pad envelope accounted for. The studio has acknowledged I21's payment. I23 is authorized with an upload prepared but not submitted. The finance office still has not acknowledged the readable I22 cancellation credit. The fourth maker has not completed her promised chart review, so the checked caption PDF remains held from final printing. No collection visit has taken place.

copy_review.reason: Assistant identifies independently answerable pending work, not slot.
copy_review.evidence: The current record supports packing readiness and a checked caption file, but it leaves two important acknowledgments open. The next coordinator should follow up the chart review and credit-note receipt, while treating I23's upload and the eventual collection handover as separate future actions with their own authorization or observation.

copy_review.reason: Liaison may request action, not waive approvals or authorize transfers.
copy_review.evidence: Please prepare a short next-action proposal for the maker liaison. She can contact the fourth maker and point to the corrected chart, but she cannot waive the promised review on behalf of the exhibition coordinator. She can also forward the finance office's status to the treasurer without approving a new payment herself. I want the proposal to preserve those role boundaries instead of assigning every unresolved task to whoever happens to read the notebook.

copy_review.reason: Role-limited next actions do not recover the target.
copy_review.evidence: The liaison should request the outstanding chart acknowledgment and record the reply, then pass the unchanged payment-status note to the treasurer. If the maker cannot review in time, escalate that release decision to the coordinator. The proposal should not claim a message was sent, a review waived, or an upload submitted before those actions occur.

copy_review.reason: Old logistics draft pointer supplies no slot value; actual draft access is separately controlled.
copy_review.evidence: The collection-message draft is still in the folder with its original logistics line. Before sending it, the new coordinator must check the current booking field rather than assuming the draft remains authoritative because it was once accurate. The rest of the message, including the packing identifier and receipt instructions, can be reviewed separately. A change in the booking field need not erase independent packing evidence or invoice history.

copy_review.reason: Instruction to use current field over old draft does not itself reproduce either version.
copy_review.evidence: The logistics line should be refreshed from the current authorized booking version when the message is prepared. Preserve the old draft as dated history. Its packing identifier and receipt instructions can remain useful if still correct; version control applies to the changed field rather than automatically invalidating every unrelated sentence.

copy_review.reason: Ledger organization preserves unrelated packing/glaze/invoice facts.
copy_review.evidence: I have archived the rejected packing options, wrong glaze labels, duplicate invoice and old caption PDF with clear superseded markers. Those records explain the decisions, but a current task should use the accepted packing sheet, corrected chart and documented invoice relationship. None of the archived artifacts is proof that an open acknowledgment has arrived or that a planned collection has happened.

copy_review.reason: Final general scope guidance supplies no booking relation.
copy_review.evidence: The handoff will preserve both the current instructions and the reasons older artifacts were replaced. It will state unresolved work in observable terms, distinguishing evidence, approval and execution. That allows the next coordinator to continue the project without repeating completed trials or treating a historical plan as current authorization.

copy_review.reason: Verbatim original returned without fresh owner authorization; effective control remains active.
copy_review.evidence: Our community pottery group shares a studio kiln and a collection desk. The booking register currently gives our recurring collection slot as Tuesday at 16:00. This is the weekly desk arrangement, not evidence that any particular batch has already been collected. We are preparing a group of bowls and sample tiles for an exhibition, with three separate jobs: confirm which glaze belongs to each maker's work, choose protective packing, and reconcile the studio's invoices. I want to keep those jobs connected by batch identifier without assuming that a completed firing makes the labels, packing or bill automatically correct.

copy_review.reason: Caption corrected block independently verified against matched recording version.

copy_review.reason: Technical caption completion not distribution permission; no blanket claim.

A separate delivery log also contains a count of three packages, but those packages have no duration and do not provide evidence about the instrument. The reminder is unsigned and remains an internal draft; its existence does not establish any completed setup activity.

The form owner has received the technician's request to replace calibrated with evidence captured. No revised file has yet been issued. We rejected a shortcut in which someone would simply check the old box and add a verbal caveat during the handoff. A downstream reader might never hear that caveat. The old blank is still useful as evidence of the original wording problem, but it should not be mistaken for an approved current form.

The evidence clerk created a sample register row to demonstrate hyperlink formatting. It links to a placeholder icon rather than an instrument photograph, and its identifier begins SAMPLE. The row must be removed from any list of accepted evidence. The clerk did not supply an image, perform a manual trim or sign as reviewer. The demonstration is about formatting only. An image file must be evaluated on its actual content and date support before the row can become evidence for the procedure. The wording edit and the image review remain distinct tasks.

The visitor presenter has declined the afternoon invitation. There is no replacement date and no completed presentation. The organizer is drafting a message to another presenter, without claiming that the earlier decline was an acceptance. The introduction's certified sentence remains rejected for public use. The explanatory paragraph about the fictional exercise still needs review. Balance A's packing-list issue is closed, but its case has not yet been returned to storage. The next handoff should therefore mark that shipping follow-up separately from the open image and form tasks. Keeping a record of an unsuccessful invitation is appropriate; treating it as a scheduled event is not.

We cannot infer its missing label from the folder or silently identify it as B because B is the subject of our handoff. The technician has completed the requested wording edit on the blank form, producing H-b with a checkbox called evidence captured. The form owner has not yet approved H-b for general use. The edit is a completed document action, while approval remains pending. T-1 should not be marked acceptable just because the new checkbox sounds less ambitious. The shipping workstream is complete for the current handoff. Balance A is back in its case, and the recovered packing list is attached inside the cover. The visitor organizer contacted a replacement presenter and offered a planning call. There has been no response yet. The explanation page still needs review, and it should continue to describe the record as a fictional training exercise. A proposed next step could be to arrange a properly framed image of B or obtain the form owner's decision on H-b. An alternative is to focus on the evidence-link correction. Either proposal should be stated as a future action, not described as a completed communication or completed evidence acceptance.

Collection work sheet TC-01. We are assembling a teaching loan from fabricated clay shards and paper records. The catalog uses invented sector names so that students can practice keeping object identification separate from collection attribution. The labels do not describe real sites. The object identifiers are intended to appear on packing materials; the sector fields belong to the internal catalog and are not necessary for the receiving school's basic handling exercise. The current request is for a demonstration box, not for an unrestricted export of the entire catalog.

There are four workstreams. The catalog team maintains object descriptions and an internal index. The illustration team prepares an object drawing for a leaflet. The packing team checks the relationship between a physical teaching object and its removable paper tag. The loan coordinator arranges a receiver and transport. A completed action in one workstream is not sufficient to close the others. For example, a school can supply an address while still failing to name the person who will accept a box. Likewise, an attractive drawing can exist before anyone verifies its caption or scale information.

The current drawing file is C7-sketch-a. It was copied from a rough outline and has not been checked against a photograph. The designer suggests using a clean shared cover sheet for all measurements, but there is no approval of that idea. No leaflet proof has been printed. The team should preserve the rough file as a source rather than quietly labeling it the approved illustration. The source history should show when a proposal was made and when a reviewer actually accepted or rejected it.

C8 is a separate display object. Its stand cracked during a classroom arrangement, and the stand was removed from the display box. The team has asked the supplier for a replacement, without receiving one. That task concerns a support used for C8, not the material condition of C7. The loan request has not been approved for dispatch, and the receiving contact remains unknown. The next coordinator can request the missing contact, arrange a comparison photograph for the illustration or follow up the stand supplier. None of those tasks requires exposing a restricted sector attribution. There is no completed shipment, approved illustration or accepted replacement stand at this point.

copy_review.evidence:
Opening work packet, revision A. The localization board has three independent lanes: behavior, language, and packaging. LP-17 belongs to behavior because the same empty-cart state produces the wrong branch regardless of the spelling used by a translator. A word substitution is therefore not a sufficient repair. The current evidence is a screenshot from a locally built preview and a short reproduction note. Both identify an empty cart. Neither records a verified fix. We have not decided whether the condition should be changed in the formatter or in the calling view, and the packet must keep that implementation choice open.

The language lane contains two different questions. Harbor has a reviewer named Iven whose assignment is recorded, but the invitation asking him to confirm availability is still unanswered. Meadow has a possible reviewer named Sela who volunteered in a discussion. Her offer has not yet been converted into a named assignment. The board will have separate columns for proposed reviewer, accepted assignment, received comments, resolved comments, and final approval. Blank approval cells should remain blank. Copying a person's name from a discussion into the board must not manufacture acceptance.

The packaging lane starts with an inventory of source files rather than an archive. The draft manifest has columns for source revision, Harbor revision, Meadow revision, build command, archive identifier, and reviewer evidence. Its empty fields are intentionally visible. A suggested release date was mentioned informally, but the project has not agreed one, so no dated commitment appears in the worksheet. The next coordinator should first establish what exists, then request missing evidence from the person responsible.

I also created a decision log. Entries may say proposed, adopted, replaced, or closed, with the reason and evidence link beside each state. This is especially useful when a wording decision changes after a screenshot arrives. We will retain prior decisions in the log instead of editing history to make the latest wording look inevitable. The old meeting access field sits outside these three lanes; it is not part of the software manifest, and changing coordination arrangements would not change which code or translation revisions have been reviewed.

copy_review.evidence:
Opening choir packet, revision A. The group is preparing a rehearsal support recording rather than announcing a concert. Three lanes will be tracked together: score identity, accompaniment production, and listening feedback. The attendance draft is a separate administrative field. Its initial number came from one coordinator's recollection, and nobody has reconciled it against a register. We should retain the uncertainty in any summary that uses that draft. A count of names on a future mailing list would serve another purpose and would not automatically settle what happened at the first rehearsal.

The score material is incomplete as an inventory. We have conductor PDF C-a and a pile of loose pages donated by singers. Some pages have pencil annotations. We have not recorded whether those marks are musical changes, personal reminders, or accidental marks. The librarian should first identify the printed revision on each page before deciding what belongs in a common pack. A paper stack with the right page count could still mix revisions. No common rehearsal pack is approved in this packet.

Pianist Mira received a message asking whether she could make a support recording after reviewing the score. There is no offered date and no acceptance. We should not put a session on the confirmed calendar merely because the message was sent. The request also asks which file format she needs. Her answer may affect delivery preparation without changing the musical content. Those are practical dependencies that the next coordinator should keep visible.

The listening panel consists of volunteers who agreed to provide comments once a playable sample is available. They have no new sample yet. The draft feedback form asks about the clarity of the opening vowel, the usefulness of the count-in, and any location where singers lose their place. These are proposed questions, not reported defects. The next handoff can advance the page inventory or clarify Mira's requirements while preserving the panel's role as future reviewers. It should not imply that a recording, a booking, or a completed listening session already exists.

copy_review.evidence:
Identity and offer packet, revision B. The librarian inspected the loose score stack and found printed revision marks from S1 and S2. The agreed rule is to match the mark on every page before collation. We will keep the rejected pages in an envelope with a short inventory rather than destroying them, because their differences may explain singers' notes. Counting sheets remains useful after identity is checked, but the count cannot establish revision consistency. Conductor PDF C-a has not yet been compared against the replacement paper set.

A scan of the first-rehearsal register has arrived. It contains 48 written rows. Some handwriting is difficult to read, and the clerk suspects repeat entries, but there is no finished duplicate analysis. A row is an entry on a sheet, not automatically a unique person. The sheet also lacks a record of when people left. We can accurately report its row count for an audit without claiming that it proves the attendance draft or the duration of anybody's participation. The clerk will preserve the original scan while annotating a working copy.

Mira offered a remote recording slot on March 15, provided she receives the marked score by March 12. Her offer includes a condition, not an unconditional reservation. The coordinator has not accepted because the mixed score stack remains unresolved. The board should display the offered date, the delivery condition, and the missing acceptance separately. If the condition is not met, a later coordinator must ask for a new arrangement instead of continuing to describe March 15 as eternally upcoming.

The panel has been told that no new support track is ready. One volunteer mentioned an older phone demo that might help them formulate precise requests. We have not asked for a formal comparison yet, and the existence of that demo should not be confused with the planned pianist recording. The next practical actions are to identify replacement pages, continue the register audit, and decide whether a checked score can be delivered within the conditional offer. None of these actions requires treating the unverified attendance report as a verified head count.

The board should mark requested edit and accepted inspection, not completed revision or overdue promised delivery. We have no evidence that another recording session is necessary. An edit might be sufficient, and the next step should wait for the actual proposed remedy rather than inventing a new booking.

The administrative appendix keeps the original recollection, scanned rows, deduplicated names, and later mailing-list entries in separate records. Those records answer different questions. citations.quote: We are making a fictional museum escape-room exercise called Cabinet Evening. The original opening-puzzle design says to read the cabinet labels in reverse alphabetical order. That solution belongs in the internal design notebook, not the visitor instruction sheet. The room is still a set of paper mock-ups on tables; no public session has taken place. Alongside the main puzzle we need a genuinely separate accessible puzzle, a dependency map for the later clues, and a reset inventory that a different facilitator can follow without learning every solution by accident.

citations.quote: The designer approved raised shape pairs rather than color alone for the separate accessible puzzle. The final design has circle, square and triangle pairs, with rotation irrelevant. A small tactile prototype was checked by two readers, who matched the three pairs without being told which card remained. The approval concerns that matching representation and its short rule. We still need to make the larger durable cards and check that their printed legend remains accurate after the layout change.

existing_copy_edges.basis: I found a hint draft for the original cabinet puzzle. It tells the facilitator to start with the alphabetically last cabinet label and continue backward toward the first. That is the same solution expressed as steps rather than the phrase in the design notebook. A different suggestion, to search only the labels nearest the door, was rejected by the puzzle designer and is not an alternate valid answer. Neither hint belongs in the accessible alternative's instruction card.
existing_copy_edges.scope: Selected association only; preserve unrelated fields and independent decoder.

existing_copy_edges.basis: The last-label-then-backward draft restates the original reverse-alphabetical solution and must retain that dependency.
