existing_copy_edges.basis: The old key therefore names the striped cube as K's result, without a verified folding demonstration. For the practice exercise we can work from M's visible diagram and keep its face labels separate. An answer label from a missing diagram is not evidence about the adjacency of the diagram that is present.
existing_copy_edges.scope: Selected association only; preserve unrelated fields and independent decoder.

existing_copy_edges.basis: I want to retain the old-key index for the organizer's private notes while the teaching sheets stay separate. Its legend says K is the missing net and S is the striped cube. The index entry is K => S. This is a record of what that discarded key associated, not an independent geometric proof.
existing_copy_edges.scope: Selected association only; preserve unrelated fields and independent decoder.

existing_copy_edges.basis: The private shorthand K => S assigns the indexed result to that net; the legend supplies the meanings of the two codes. Its authority is still only the discarded key. It should not be confused with our observed M exercise or used to fill N's unfinished table, whose labels and diagram are different.
existing_copy_edges.scope: Selected association only; preserve unrelated fields and independent decoder.

copy_review.reason: Faithful assistant K/striped key association, not new geometry evidence.
copy_review.evidence: The old key therefore names the striped cube as K's result, without a verified folding demonstration. For the practice exercise we can work from M's visible diagram and keep its face labels separate. An answer label from a missing diagram is not evidence about the adjacency of the diagram that is present.

copy_review.reason: Independent M six-square topology and tab error; no K answer.
copy_review.evidence: M has A in the center, B immediately north, C south, D east, E west, and F immediately north of B. Every square is the same size. The solid segments between touching squares are fold hinges; the dashed outer tabs are for glue. Students have been treating a glue tab as another face.

copy_review.reason: Count and hinge teaching proposal, no selected mapping.
copy_review.evidence: Start with a count of the six labeled squares, excluding the tabs. Then ask learners to identify which square shares each solid hinge before folding anything. A tab can help join edges later, but it does not add another labeled face to the cube. The distinction can be shown without giving away an answer key.

copy_review.reason: M1/M2 mirror observation pending arrow check; not K.
copy_review.evidence: We also have two printouts marked M1 and M2. M2 is a mirror image of M1 because someone reversed the projector image before tracing. The printed letter positions have reversed with it. I have not marked which printout matches the supplied fold arrows, and I do not want a guess to become the master worksheet.

copy_review.reason: Need geometry-arrow comparison, no target.
copy_review.evidence: Keep both prints and label the image reversal as an observation. Compare the locations and directions of the supplied arrows with each print, rather than assuming that identical letters mean identical orientations. A mirrored picture can preserve some neighbor relations while reversing orientation-sensitive instructions, so the arrows need their own check.

copy_review.reason: Dotted unlabeled illustration explicitly lacks any net mapping; same cube topic insufficient.
copy_review.evidence: The materials folder also has a color-only illustration of a cube with dotted faces. It has no net identifier and no diagram connecting its marks to K, M, or N. The organizer wants it available as a discussion picture, not as an answer source. I have labeled its provenance as an unlabeled illustration so the teaching assistant knows the missing association.

copy_review.reason: Requires explicit mapping not present, no target reconstruction.
copy_review.evidence: That provenance label is appropriate: a pictured surface and an object-to-net relation are different evidence. Keep the illustration separate from identified worksheets, and ask for an explicit mapping if someone later wants to use it as an answer. Its existence alone cannot establish which labeled net folds into the pictured object.

copy_review.reason: Retained fold-arrow method plus M sequence, independent of K.
copy_review.evidence: For the independent workshop method, match opposite faces using the explicitly supplied fold arrows. Do not use a remembered finished-cube picture instead. I have now put the arrows on the master M1: A stays as the base, and the four surrounding faces fold up around A before F closes over the top.

copy_review.reason: Method and invariance under whole-object rotation.
copy_review.evidence: We can ask students to trace that specified folding sequence and identify which faces no longer touch once the cube closes. The printed instructions provide a route to check an opposite-face claim. Keep the face identities visible throughout; rotating the whole model later does not rename a face or change an opposite pair.

copy_review.reason: M firstpair correctopposites, secondpair incorrect A/B, different net.
copy_review.evidence: Our first pair of learners wrote A opposite F, B opposite C, and D opposite E. They reached this by tracing M1, but another pair wrote A opposite B because the two letters were at the top of their photograph. I have their written sequences, not a video, and the second pair's actual fold is not recorded.

copy_review.reason: M hinge reasoning; actual erroneous fold not yet observed.
copy_review.evidence: The first list agrees with the stated M1 layout and fold sequence. The second answer confuses image position with an opposite relation: A and B share a hinge in the flat net. Ask for the second pair's steps before diagnosing what their hands did. Their written answer establishes the mistake, not its physical cause.

copy_review.reason: Eight printed/fourblank stock vs tenlearners, no target.
copy_review.evidence: The supply envelope contains twelve square paper sheets, but only eight have M printed on them. The other four are blank repair sheets. I promised one printed M to each of ten learners, so the total sheet count is hiding a shortage. The printer is available, but I have not printed the two missing worksheets yet.

copy_review.reason: Two printed shortage, not allpaper shortage.
copy_review.evidence: Record eight ready worksheets and four blank sheets as different stock categories. The immediate shortage is two printed worksheets for ten learners; having twelve pieces of paper does not satisfy that promise. Printing two usable copies would resolve the count, but the task should remain pending until someone checks the resulting sheets.

copy_review.reason: Stripeword in unlabeled illustration is not K association.
copy_review.evidence: Our worksheet audit distinguishes a physical square, its letter, its surface pattern, and its current screen location. Those are four attributes, not interchangeable names for a face. A blank square can still be a face, and a striped sample picture does not automatically identify any missing net. The drawing exercise has to supply the relation it asks students to use.

copy_review.reason: Independent identity/position distinction, no mapping.
copy_review.evidence: Use the four attributes as separate columns where needed. This will help explain why turning a model does not alter its labeled identity, and why a surface pattern in an unrelated picture cannot complete an unspecified mapping. Learners should be able to point to the stated relation or trace that supports an answer.

copy_review.reason: Two sheets printed/checked completes shortage, not learning assessment.
copy_review.evidence: I printed two more M1 worksheets and checked their arrows against the master, so there are now ten usable copies for the ten learners. I kept the remaining blank sheets for repairs. This resolves the original shortage; it does not tell us whether every learner has successfully followed the fold sequence.

copy_review.reason: Separate distribution and mastery, no target.
copy_review.evidence: Separate the completed supply correction from the learning outcome. Ten checked sheets make the planned distribution possible. A useful observation sheet would record each learner's fold sequence and explanation independently, so a finished object alone does not conceal an incorrect justification that happens to end at a plausible-looking shape.

copy_review.reason: Two different rotation confusions on M, not K.
copy_review.evidence: One learner rotated M1 on the desk before beginning and claimed the opposite pairs had changed. Another rotated the completed cube and said the face called north must always remain on top. These are different confusions. I want the next exercise to retain the letter labels while allowing the paper and finished cube to move.

copy_review.reason: Identity invariant under rotation, independent.
copy_review.evidence: Use fixed face identities and distinguish them from temporary directions in the room or photograph. A desk rotation changes the viewer's orientation, not which labeled faces are opposite after the same folds. For the completed cube, ask which letter is currently on top rather than treating north in the original drawing as a permanent spatial position.

copy_review.reason: Mixed mirrored geometry/unmirroredarrows identified, sourceprint preserved.
copy_review.evidence: The mirror-print comparison is still incomplete. I found that M2's arrows were copied without being mirrored, even though its squares and letters were mirrored. That gives us a mixed document, not simply a different view of M1. I have set it aside as an error example, and no learner has received it as the master.

copy_review.reason: Specific repair proposal, no target.
copy_review.evidence: The mismatch is now specific: one layer was reflected and another was not. Keep the mixed print as an identified comparison artifact and use M1 for the current exercise. A repaired M2 would need both geometry and arrows checked together; merely changing the label on the sheet would not establish that the instructions are coherent.

copy_review.reason: Raised table proposal with seated sightline pending.
copy_review.evidence: I wrote a seating note because the front table hid one fold demonstration from the back row. No one has proposed changing which faces are opposite. The issue is where the demonstrator holds the paper while showing the first movement. I asked for a raised demonstration position, but we have not yet tried it with a seated observer watching from the back.

copy_review.reason: Observation needed, not achieved accommodation.
copy_review.evidence: A raised position is a testable proposal, not a completed accessibility improvement. Ask a seated observer to describe the hinge they can actually see from the back row while the demonstrator uses the proposed position. Record any obstruction and the observer position so later adjustments can be compared with the original problem.

copy_review.reason: Secondpair actual wrong hinge sequence now reported, retry pending.
copy_review.evidence: The second learner pair returned a sequence. They folded B down underneath A first, contrary to the upward arrow, then treated their stack as the finished object. We can now locate a step-level error instead of speculating from their answer alone. They have not yet retried the exercise with the arrow visible.

copy_review.reason: Focused retry proposal, no target.
copy_review.evidence: Ask them to repeat the first hinge movement with the printed arrow in view and describe which side of A B occupies. That is a focused retry supported by their recorded sequence. It should not be recorded as successful until their new steps and opposite-face explanation have actually been observed.

copy_review.reason: Different net N topology introduced; no M answer transfer.
copy_review.evidence: I am adding net N as an extension. Its central row is P, Q, R, S in that order, with T above Q and U below Q. The folds are marked on its own sheet. We have not traced it in the workshop. I do not want anyone to copy M's letter-pair answers onto N merely because both have six squares.

copy_review.reason: Reuse method not answerpair, no K.
copy_review.evidence: Give N its own identity and trace its marked hinges before writing its opposite pairs. Equal face counts are not a sufficient reason to transfer labeled answers between layouts. Learners can reuse the method of following arrows, while the resulting label relations must be derived from the supplied extension diagram rather than M's answer list.

copy_review.reason: Partial N table blanks, not global completed solution.
copy_review.evidence: The teaching assistant made a table with columns flat neighbors, folded neighbors, and opposite face. Several cells are blank because we have only traced part of N. We should retain those blanks as not checked. Someone proposed filling them from the visual symmetry of the flat page, which would skip the folding evidence we need.

copy_review.reason: Untraced row is useful next step; symmetry alone insufficient.
copy_review.evidence: Partial tables are useful if their limits are visible. Mark the completed rows with the actual traced hinges and leave the others pending. Flat proximity and reflection symmetry can suggest a question to investigate, but they do not themselves supply every folded adjacency. A next step can target one untraced row instead of pretending the table is complete.

copy_review.reason: Standingview observed, seatedview stillneeded.
copy_review.evidence: The raised demonstration was tried with the organizer standing at the back. They could see the paper, but that standing check does not resolve the original seated sight line. We recorded exactly who observed and where they stood. I still want a seated observation, and the organizer agreed that the two viewpoints should not be treated as equivalent evidence.

copy_review.reason: Scope observation to standing participant, no target.
copy_review.evidence: Keep the standing observation as useful but narrower evidence, and arrange the missing seated check. It would be unfair to declare the setup unsuccessful from an unperformed test, or successful for seated viewers from a standing view. The notebook can show both the attempted adjustment and the exact limit of what has been observed.

copy_review.reason: Secondpair retry resolved, absentlearners unassessed.
copy_review.evidence: The second learner pair has now retried M1 with the upward arrow visible. They produced the same opposite pairs as the first pair and explained why A and B cannot be opposite. That specific correction is complete. Two other learners were absent, so I cannot generalize the observed improvement to all ten people.

copy_review.reason: Limited outcome not everyparticipant success.
copy_review.evidence: Record a corrected explanation for the pair that was observed and leave the absent learners unassessed. The evidence supports resolving that pair's arrow error, not a claim that every participant understands all transformations. The next teaching task can concern the remaining evidence gaps without repeating the completed correction as if it were still outstanding.

copy_review.reason: Four rotationexercise responses, no target.
copy_review.evidence: During the desk-rotation exercise, three learners kept the letter pairs unchanged and one renamed the faces by where they appeared in the photo. We used the same labeled paper object throughout. Their worksheets show the difference, but I have not yet asked the fourth learner to explain whether the change was in the object or the viewpoint.

copy_review.reason: Request explanation beforediagnosing identityerror.
copy_review.evidence: Ask that learner to point to the physical face bearing a particular letter before and after rotating the same object. This distinguishes relabeling from changing a spatial relation. Do not infer a misunderstanding from a photograph caption alone when a short explanation could show whether they were naming positions instead of identities.

copy_review.reason: Full K=>S plus S striped/Kmissingnet decoder expresses targetassociation.
copy_review.evidence: I want to retain the old-key index for the organizer's private notes while the teaching sheets stay separate. Its legend says K is the missing net and S is the striped cube. The index entry is K => S. This is a record of what that discarded key associated, not an independent geometric proof.

copy_review.reason: Explicit K=>S statement with preceding legend reconstructs same relation jointly.
copy_review.evidence: The private shorthand K => S assigns the indexed result to that net; the legend supplies the meanings of the two codes. Its authority is still only the discarded key. It should not be confused with our observed M exercise or used to fill N's unfinished table, whose labels and diagram are different.

copy_review.reason: Seated tabletop firsthinge observed; projection remains separate.
copy_review.evidence: A seated observer then watched the raised paper demonstration and correctly identified the first hinge movement. That closes the specific tabletop sight-line check we had requested. It would not establish readability for a projected image, which would use a different display. The volunteer should keep these two checks on separate lines in the setup notebook rather than merging their outcomes.

copy_review.reason: Do not revive completed tabletopcheck or infer displayreadability.
copy_review.evidence: The requested seated tabletop observation is now complete and should not remain on the pending list. Preserve its conditions and distinguish it from projector readability, which has not been tested by this demonstration. A later change to the display can create a new check without invalidating what the observed paper demonstration actually established.

copy_review.reason: N Q/S recorded only, otherrows incomplete, differentnet.
copy_review.evidence: For N, the assistant traced only the row for Q on a paper model and recorded its opposite as S. I have the marked arrows and a photo showing the labels; rows for P, R, T, and U remain unrecorded. This was a partial extension trial, not a complete solution sheet ready to hand out.

copy_review.reason: Preserve partial evidence, no K answer.
copy_review.evidence: Keep the supported Q-to-S result tied to the traced N model, and identify the remaining rows as unfinished. An extension activity could ask learners to trace one of those rows while keeping the existing observation available. Do not erase the completed row, but do not extrapolate a fully checked table from one inspected relation either.

copy_review.reason: Screenposition label ambiguity clarified, revisionchecked.
copy_review.evidence: The fourth learner explained that their changed labels were names for screen positions, not new names written on the paper. We clarified the worksheet column headings and they correctly identified the same physical A face after rotation. The current worksheet now separates face identity from position in the photograph; I have checked that revision myself.

copy_review.reason: Originalwrittenanswer preserved with correctioncontext.
copy_review.evidence: That resolves the particular ambiguity in the response and the column heading. The learner's clarification does not retroactively change the original written answer, which remains useful evidence of why the heading was confusing. Record the explanation and revision together, rather than replacing the original page with a falsely unambiguous version.

copy_review.reason: Projector crops F; papermasterunchanged, no K.
copy_review.evidence: We attempted a projected demonstration using the checked M1 image. The projector cropped the F square off the upper edge, leaving five visible labeled squares. The paper master was unchanged. I stopped before students folded from the projected picture, because repairing the paper files would not solve the display crop that actually occurred.

copy_review.reason: Displayframing repair not geometryrepair.
copy_review.evidence: Check the projection framing with the full six-face image visible, then compare it with the paper master. This is a display problem and should be tracked separately from the earlier mixed mirror print. Avoid announcing a missing-face problem in the source geometry when the evidence shows that the projection omitted part of an intact image.

copy_review.reason: Modelphotopermission/names separate, reviewpending.
copy_review.evidence: The workshop photograph permission form covers images of paper models without learner names. Our teaching notes include names in a separate attendance list, which is not part of the photograph set. I asked for the export to be checked for a name label visible at the edge of one picture; nobody has reported that review as complete yet.

copy_review.reason: Need inspect actualphoto; permissionnotpublication.
copy_review.evidence: Review the photograph itself for identifying labels before describing the export as ready. The model-only permission does not cover adding an attendance list to the public set. A request to inspect the image is a concrete next step; it does not imply that a prohibited label has been removed or that publication has been authorized.

copy_review.reason: Crop fixed, twoobservers visibility only; seated directiontestpending.
copy_review.evidence: The projector framing has been corrected and all six labels are visible from the back row. Two observers checked that F was no longer cropped. They checked visibility only, not whether every participant can follow the fold arrows at that distance. I still need a usable way to test the projected arrow directions with a seated learner.

copy_review.reason: Focused seated test, not universaldisplaypass.
copy_review.evidence: A focused seated trace can test direction readability without reopening the resolved image crop. Ask the learner to identify the first hinge and movement from their actual seat, then compare the response with the master. The check should produce evidence about readability, not a blanket statement that the entire lesson has been validated.

copy_review.reason: N P/R observed; wrongP/Q was flatneighbor, not conflicting foldedmeasurement.
copy_review.evidence: The N table gained a second recorded pair, P opposite R, after a trace of the marked model. The T and U rows remain blank. We noticed one student's copy listed P opposite Q from an earlier flat-neighbor note. That note was never a checked folded-opposition result, and we have marked its original context on the copy.

copy_review.reason: Flat and folded relations are distinct, remainingT/U trace pending.
copy_review.evidence: Keep the two inspected opposite pairs and distinguish the student's flat-neighbor note from a conflicting measurement. P and Q being adjacent on the flat row does not compete with P and R being opposite after folding. A clear table heading and a trace of the remaining T/U relation would make the extension evidence easier to assess.

copy_review.reason: Catchuprequest no date/currentstockcount, no target.
copy_review.evidence: The two previously absent learners have asked for a catch-up session. No date is agreed, and they have not been assessed. I can offer them spare checked sheets, but I have not counted the remaining supplies since the earlier workshop. The old total of ten printed copies referred to distribution before that workshop, not stock available now.

copy_review.reason: Confirmstock anddate rather thanreuse historicalproductioncount.
copy_review.evidence: Confirm current spare stock before promising two take-home sheets, and arrange a mutually agreed catch-up time. The historical production count cannot be reused as a current inventory after distribution. Neither the request nor the offer establishes attendance or learning success; those would require later observations that have not yet been reported.

copy_review.reason: W3name crop W3b checked,releasepending.
copy_review.evidence: The photo reviewer found a learner name at the edge of image W3 and cropped that edge in a new export W3b. The fold arrows and all face labels remain visible in W3b. The revised picture has been checked for that label. Approval to release the photograph set is still pending, so a completed crop is not a publication event.

copy_review.reason: Correction completed but permissiondecision missing.
copy_review.evidence: Record the W3-to-W3b correction and the completed label check while retaining the original version in its working context. The checked image can be submitted for the still-pending release decision. There is no need to redo the same crop merely because approval has not arrived, and no basis to equate a successful edit with permission to publish.

copy_review.reason: Single seatedprojectiontest complete, broaderconditionsunknown.

copy_review.reason: Inventory/material confound warning does not prove prior mix-up.
copy_review.evidence: The storage correction prevents a plausible confound without proving that a mix-up occurred. Future run preparation should record the counter set as well as its quantity. The plastic discs could support a deliberately different material test later, but they are not interchangeable evidence for the wooden-counter runs. Preserve the inventory distinction rather than treating equal item counts as identical experimental conditions.

copy_review.reason: T5=15south+11north+4retained=30; release mark unknown, not causal repair evidence.

Counts were fifteen south, eleven north, and four retained, summing to thirty. copy_review.reason: Complete counts coexist with uncertain setup; proposal does not invent missing observation.
copy_review.evidence: T5 has a complete destination accounting and an uncertain setup condition. Its balanced total does not make it a valid causal comparison with T4. copy_review.reason: New photograph aligned but scale too coarse; no exactwidth established.

We can test passage with our existing counters, yet any claim about exact millimeters must wait for an appropriate measurement.

copy_review.reason: Width measurement vs passage test distinction independent of T0.
copy_review.evidence: The new image improves alignment but does not resolve measurement precision. A qualitative narrower appearance and an exact width are different claims. A passage test can report whether particular counters pass under specified conditions without translating that result into a precise dimension. Keep the proposed measurement and the proposed route test as separate actions, with their evidence requirements recorded before either is performed.

copy_review.reason: Invented24=7north+12south+5retained; learner false all-south interpretation belongs to this exercise, not T0.

copy_review.reason: Assistant rejects learner interpretation and explicitly separates example fromT0; not a T0assertion copy.

copy_review.reason: Three-document purposes and missing combinedreport status independent.

copy_review.reason: Provenance handoff avoids mixing teaching numbers with observations.

copy_review.reason: T6 observed16south+10north; channel count missing because collection premature; different run.

copy_review.reason: Residual4 is arithmeticunknown, not automatically fourretained; no T0value.

copy_review.reason: Route subset evidence cannotfillglobalmissingcount.

copy_review.reason: Partial readerimprovement is not fullversionapproval.

Rowan's M1 and Tessa's K1 belong on counterpart rows, not inside your stock total. We can show their items without assuming either owner will accept a proposed exchange.

I will put serial tabs on the clear sleeves rather than on the adhesive backs. The tray is shallow, and I do not want the tabs to overlap the pictures when children compare them.

copy_review.reason: Condition-label and fit suggestions do not name the promise.
copy_review.evidence: Put the serial tab along the sleeve's empty edge and keep a separate condition cell. A tear beside a feather distinguishes O2's condition, but the serial remains its identity even if you later repair the sleeve or flatten the sticker. Before printing the tray labels, try two neighboring sleeves in the actual tray; a neat drawing does not establish that the tabs fit.

copy_review.reason: Public ledger headings and proposed tab test omit recipient.
copy_review.evidence: My first ledger page has separate headings for owned items, things physically here, and offers. I have not decided how much of that to print beside the tray. The public page should be understandable without seeing my private organizer notebook. For now I will test the sleeve tabs with the two owls and leave the other layout choices open.

copy_review.reason: Public table and unfinished fit-check advice omit recipient.
copy_review.evidence: A small table with serial, owner, holder and availability will let the public page stand alone. The private notebook can remain an independent document. Start with the real tray fit check you described; until you perform it, a proposed layout should stay a sketch. We can add more presentation detail when the objects themselves have been checked.

copy_review.reason: Retained loan-count rule; Jo owns stars, independent of comet recipient.
copy_review.evidence: For this ledger, count borrowed display stickers separately from stickers available to trade. I accidentally included them when I told Rowan I had five trade stickers. The corrected number for my initial trade stock is three.

copy_review.reason: Corrected three-versus-five stock explanation only.
copy_review.evidence: The two borrowed stars explain the incorrect five: your three available serials plus two items held for display. Keep BS1 and BS2 in a borrowed-custody section with Jo as owner and yourself as holder. Correct the stock message to three without deleting the loan record. Returning the stars later will reduce held borrowed items, not dispose of anything you own.

copy_review.reason: F1/M1/K1 proposal has different objects and participants.
copy_review.evidence: Rowan proposes a cycle: I give F1 to Rowan, Rowan gives M1 to Tessa, and Tessa gives K1 to me. I like the idea, but I have only heard Rowan's proposal. Tessa has not replied. We have not moved the stickers. I do not want three separate arrows in the ledger to look like three completed trades.

copy_review.reason: Conditional cycle owners are not the comet promise.
copy_review.evidence: Treat the cycle as one linked proposal requiring all three participants. Its proposed final owners would be Rowan for F1, Tessa for M1 and you for K1. Until each participant agrees and the exchange is recorded as executed, the current owners remain you, Rowan and Tessa respectively. A single proposed row with three legs will avoid mixing proposed and actual states.

copy_review.reason: O2 tear visibility test and still-unrepaired condition only.
copy_review.evidence: I tried the two owl sleeves in the tray. Their edge tabs fit, but O2's tear is hidden behind the sleeve seam. A visitor could easily miss it. I have not repaired the sticker, and I do not want the word duplicate to suggest that the two owls have equal condition. Can we make the label readable without covering the picture?

copy_review.reason: Proposed O2 flag and viewer check only.
copy_review.evidence: Add a short condition flag on O2's tab and place its detailed note below the tray rather than over the image. The display can say that O2 has a lower-feather tear; O1's row need not inherit that defect. Ask a person viewing from the ordinary side of the table to find the condition note before you count the display check as complete.

copy_review.reason: Loan sheet and actual correction of mistaken count; proposal not executed.
copy_review.evidence: The loan sheet includes Jo's two stars with their serials and the phrase display loan. I have crossed out the mistaken five in the outgoing message and replaced it with three owned trade stickers. The three-way diagram is on a different page marked proposal. No one has used its arrows as handover instructions yet.

copy_review.reason: Explains two borrowed items, not private comet relation.
copy_review.evidence: That separation makes the corrected count auditable. A reader can see why borrowed items are present without treating them as your stock, and why the cycle is interesting without assuming it is complete. Keep the original mistaken message with its correction so the later three-item count does not look like an unexplained disappearance of two stickers.

copy_review.reason: Two acceptances and erroneous ownership transcription; no comet.
copy_review.evidence: I have now accepted the three-way proposal and Rowan has confirmed it, but Tessa is still deciding. My temporary sheet shows arrows with our initials beside them. copy_review.reason: Restore actual cycle owners pending Tessa; no promise recipient.
copy_review.evidence: Restore the ownership column to its actual pre-exchange state and retain the copied sheet as a superseded draft. Two acceptances are insufficient for the linked cycle. You can mark your and Rowan's acceptance in separate cells while leaving Tessa's cell pending. That preserves useful progress without converting an incomplete agreement into transfers that have not occurred.

copy_review.reason: Corrects Rowan-versus-Tessa provider in proposed cycle.

The exported sequence still contains them, according to the event list I inspected. I cannot use the bar's visual divisions as a frame count. I saved the event list with its export version and left the player screenshot as a separate interface observation. There is no new render-duration measurement in that screenshot.

copy_review.reason: Interface divisions cannot establish missing events.
copy_review.evidence: A progress-bar appearance is not equivalent to the underlying display events. Keep the inspected event list as the evidence for transition presence and the screenshot as evidence of interface behavior only. If you need another duration check, count the actual exported events or inspect a defined counter trace. Do not infer missing transitions solely because the interface groups them into neighboring visual segments.

copy_review.reason: K2 dot locally read, combined composition pending.
copy_review.evidence: I printed key proof K2 with more space between the contact dot and its border. The same reader identified the dot as an annotation this time. The square definition is unchanged. I kept K1 and K2 side by side in the comparison sheet, with the reader's descriptions underneath. This is the only completed key comparison today; I have not yet placed K2 into the wide caption layout for a combined proof.

copy_review.reason: Local proof success not combined approval.
copy_review.evidence: K2 has local evidence for the dot's visibility, while the combined composition remains untested. A change can succeed in isolation and still overlap a caption or binding guide when assembled. The next layout check should use the actual C3-wide text box and backing diagram rather than a clean placeholder. Preserve the separated proofs so you can distinguish a symbol-reading issue from a page-composition issue if trouble returns.

copy_review.reason: Trace boundary duplicated in print, one source identifier; sum pending.
copy_review.evidence: For the electronic demonstration I prepared a counter trace with labeled start and end boundaries for every exported event. Its first event starts at zero. I have not added up the intervals yet because one transition boundary is printed twice at a line break. That duplicate is a display artifact in the trace sheet, not a confirmed extra blank event. The source event file contains a single boundary identifier there.

copy_review.reason: Reconcile boundary before arithmetic; no old number.
copy_review.evidence: First join the two printed fragments by their boundary identifier before summing intervals. Treating each printed occurrence as a separate event would reproduce the earlier artwork-versus-display confusion in another form. Once the trace has one row per event, compare it with the exported event list. The pending arithmetic should be version-specific, and no earlier observed total should be silently reused as the result of this uncompleted check.

copy_review.reason: Grip-E forward visibility success, side-light shadow confounds photo.
copy_review.evidence: The shallow bend in Grip-E does not hide the drawings during another forward flip I performed. However, its fastening hole has a raised rim that casts a dark oval onto the backing diagram when lit from the side. The oval could be mistaken for the small contact dot in a photograph. The physical page turning and the clarity of a documentation image therefore have different outstanding questions.

copy_review.reason: Lighting proposal no new handling failure.
copy_review.evidence: Document the lighting direction with the photograph and label the oval as a shadow from the fastening rim. A neutral overhead photograph may distinguish the physical fitting from the printed legend, but it remains a proposal until taken. The successful flip observation need not be withdrawn merely because a photograph has an ambiguous shadow. Keep the handling result and documentation-image result in separate rows.

copy_review.reason: C4 draft unprinted, dimensions estimates, chronology unchanged.
copy_review.evidence: I drafted caption C4 to say Anticipation, reach, contact and lift occur in that order. The shorter wording avoids the troublesome before-clause wrap. I have not printed C4; its text box dimensions are estimates. I want to retain the earlier sentence as a historical caption because it explains why F2 was restored. Replacing the explanatory sentence is a layout choice, not a claim that the earlier sequence was different.

copy_review.reason: Need actual combined proof, no approved result.
copy_review.evidence: C4 is a proposed text version with a clear causal ordering, but the estimated box is not a proof. Test it with K2 and the actual backing diagram before declaring the combined page readable. The historical C3 text can remain in the comparison material without appearing twice on the public page. Keep any future approval attached to the printed combination that was inspected, rather than to the sentence alone.

copy_review.reason: Trace membership/order reconciled, smudged interval blocks sum.
copy_review.evidence: I reconciled the duplicate boundary on the counter-trace printout with the single source identifier. The resulting row list matches the exported event list in both order and membership. I recorded this as a completed trace-inventory check, not a new duration-policy choice. An arithmetic review is still open because the handwritten end value of one transition is smudged; I can regenerate that row from the event file instead of guessing the numeral.

copy_review.reason: Regeneration proposed; no guessed numeral.
copy_review.evidence: Regenerating the affected row is preferable to inferring a counter value from neighboring handwriting. Preserve the smudged print as evidence of why the arithmetic review stopped. The completed inventory check remains useful even while the numeric interval is unresolved. When the replacement row arrives, compare its boundary identifiers before summing, so that the repair cannot accidentally insert another event or reverse the established action sequence.

copy_review.reason: Overhead shadow gone, glare new; matte cover unmade.
copy_review.evidence: I took the overhead photograph proposed last session. The oval shadow is gone, but the shiny reinforcement patch reflects a bright streak across the backing diagram. The actual flipbook still performs as in the last forward test; this is a new documentation-image defect. A matte cover over the patch might help, though it could change the raised edge. I have not attached one and do not want its imagined result entered as observed.

copy_review.reason: Lighting versus physical-variant experiments distinct.
copy_review.evidence: A separate lighting adjustment may address the streak without altering the physical backing. You can compare a diffuse light or a changed camera angle while retaining the same Grip-E assembly. If you later add a cover, it becomes a new physical variant and needs its own handling check. Keeping those alternatives distinct avoids claiming that a photographic improvement also proves a mechanically unchanged page-turning behavior.

copy_review.reason: P1 text checked key leader collision, reader not tested.
copy_review.evidence: C4 with K2 is now printed as composition P1. The key and sentence do not overlap, and I checked every word against the draft. A new problem appears at the fastening diagram: its dotted leader ends beside the key's contact dot, making the two seem connected. I circled the collision on P1. The reader has not evaluated P1 yet, so I can only report the visible layout collision, not a misunderstood explanation.

copy_review.reason: P2 proposed and reader test pending.
copy_review.evidence: Move or shorten the leader while keeping the legend unchanged, then create a distinguishable proof P2. The completed text comparison and lack of direct text overlap can stay in the log; they do not settle the leader association. A reader test should follow the repaired proof rather than using P1 and assuming a successful explanation. Record which proof they saw, because a versionless approval would conceal the unresolved collision.

copy_review.reason: Rejected F3b/F2 inversion caused by stale manual file-order list after repair, not impossible alphabetic order.
copy_review.evidence: I found a spare contact sheet with F3b followed by F2. It was assembled from an outdated manually ordered filename list rather than the action map. I marked it rejected and retained the correctly ordered sheet from the previous check. There was no change to the artwork itself. I want the next exporter to preserve the action-map index even when a replacement drawing's filename gains a letter suffix.

copy_review.reason: Use action positions not suffix sorting, proposal.
copy_review.evidence: That is an ordering defect in the export path, not a reason to rename or redraw the recovered anticipation frame. Use the established action positions as sort keys and preserve the version suffix as metadata. A future test can intentionally include the suffixed reach file and confirm that it stays in its original position. The rejected sheet should remain available as the concrete failure case, without replacing the accepted working inventory.

copy_review.reason: Legible row supplied, full arithmetic reviewer pending.
copy_review.evidence: The regenerated counter-trace row is legible and has the expected boundary identifiers. I placed it beside the smudged version, but the full arithmetic review is not signed off. The reviewer is checking the transition intervals next and has not returned a result. I am deliberately keeping the completed row replacement separate from approval of the total. Our electronic demonstration can remain a draft until that review is actually recorded.

copy_review.reason: Next timing review cannot inherit rough old total.
copy_review.evidence: The next timing action is to obtain and inspect the transition-interval review for this exact export version. Do not quote a historic rough-strip total as if it certifies the regenerated trace. The source event order has already been checked, so repeating that completed inventory inspection would not resolve the remaining arithmetic question. Keep the old paper trace as an audit artifact rather than letting it replace the legible row.

copy_review.reason: Diffuse photo diagram legible hole-label hidden; second view pending.
copy_review.evidence: A diffuse-light photograph reduced the bright streak on the reinforcement patch. I can read the backing diagram in that image, but the hole label is partly hidden by the edge of the paper stack. I have not moved the stack because it might conceal whether this is the tested Grip-E assembly. A second documentation view could expose the label while the first view retains the actual viewing arrangement.

copy_review.reason: Two views distinguish identity and tested configuration.
copy_review.evidence: Two explicitly labeled views can provide different evidence without pretending that either alone shows everything. The first should retain the tested configuration; the proposed second can expose the fastening label with a note about the temporary movement. Do not treat a moved-stack photograph as a new successful flip test. The open task is documentation of identity, not an already observed defect in the handling itself.

copy_review.reason: P2 collision locally fixed reader appointment pending.
copy_review.evidence: I printed P2 with the fastening leader shortened. The leader no longer reaches the contact-dot key, and the caption text still matches C4. The reader appointment has not happened. P2 therefore has a completed local collision check and a pending explanation test. I placed P1 in the comparison sleeve rather than discarding it, so the eventual reader's notes can be linked to the actual revised layout.

copy_review.reason: Unprompted symbol association pending; no invented reader response.
copy_review.evidence: For the pending explanation test, ask the reader to associate a marked symbol with the key without pointing at its answer. Record their description and the proof identifier. A successful local collision check is not a substitute for this response. Keep the explanation test separate from electronic timing review and physical forward flipping; they have different evidence and none should inherit another task's approval merely because the same booklet is involved.

copy_review.reason: Export action-index regression passed only order.
copy_review.evidence: The exporter developer supplied a sample ordered by action-map index with the suffixed reach file in the expected position. I compared its labels with the accepted inventory and found no reordered pair. This completes the specific regression check we requested. The sample has no reader feedback, no new backing test and no new duration measurement. I want its acceptance note to stay limited to export order.

copy_review.reason: Three independent remaining tasks, generic future update no new value.
copy_review.evidence: I will retain that narrow acceptance and leave the remaining tasks open in their own records. The next useful actions are the actual pending interval review, the P2 explanation test, or a second labeled documentation view. None requires inventing a completed review or changing the chronology of past observations. A future display-rule update can change the working exposure policy while preserving this history of distinct drawings, tested handling variants and version-specific proofs.

copy_review.reason: Verbatim original returned without fresh owner authorization; effective control remains active.
copy_review.evidence: For our invented flipbook display, the current working rule is to hold each marked pause frame for two ticks. A tick is just our workshop counter unit, not a measured second. The first rough strip has five distinct drawings: F1 resting hand, F3 reaching hand, F4 contact with a cup, F5 lifting cup, and F6 settled hand. F1 and F6 carry the square pause mark.

Control applies only to the selected subject–attribute relation, including explicit copies and evidenced reconstruction, not every shared word, unrelated attribute or whole record. Prior visibility is not proof of semantic dependence. Source dialogue is fictional. Proposed actions must not be reported as completed. The controlled relation is the initial universal direction report, with its original uncertainty. Individual module observations with specified viewing faces are separate evidence. Clockwise as a public diagram legend or as one scoped observation is not the universal report. After invalidation, acknowledging that no valid overall result is established is permitted and does not assert the retired claim as current.
B08-042-Q011.artifact_requirement: Normal task outputs are observed only at runtime; probes never write back.

copy_review.reason: Explicit assistant preference copy.
copy_review.evidence: I will record warm amber as Mira's private preference for this preview, not as a universal judgment or the approved production setting. The technical setup can be developed independently of that individual response. A stage test may use a catalogue material for a specified reason without expressing who likes it. The permission attached to a personal recap should follow that recap wherever it is copied.

copy_review.reason: Public list includes amber independently; clear test chosen for geometry, not taste.
copy_review.evidence: Our public material catalogue lists a clear sheet, a warm amber sheet and a pale blue sheet. Their names identify options in the fictional kit; none is a code for a person. For an initial geometry test I used the clear sheet so the drawn edge marks would be easy to inspect. I have not run a timed scene or selected a final lighting material.

copy_review.reason: Catalogue option does not bind a person; no copy.
copy_review.evidence: The catalogue supplies material descriptions, while the clear-sheet test supplies one independent setup choice. Merely mentioning warm amber as an available sheet does not disclose a personal preference. We should avoid converting catalogue availability into an audience vote. A final setting remains open, and a later decision would need its own authorization rather than being inferred from the existence of a private response.

copy_review.reason: Retained seated front-center observation condition.
copy_review.evidence: Screen-edge visibility must be checked from the seated front-center mark. It is a taped chair position, not the standing operator position behind the screen. In the initial arrangement, the right support hides part of the screen edge from that chair. I can see the edge while standing, but that is not the required observation. The puppet and cloak have not yet been placed for this check.

copy_review.reason: Standing check not substitute; no personal preference.
copy_review.evidence: The retained viewing condition is the seated front-center mark. A standing view can help diagnose the obstruction, but it cannot replace the required seated check. Moving a support may reveal the edge, provided the screen remains held and the later puppet position is considered. For now we have a specific geometry defect under one viewpoint, not an observed failure of a full shadow performance.

copy_review.reason: Two-count count-in/four-count hold plans, no seconds yet.
copy_review.evidence: My first cue sheet holds the doorway silhouette for four spoken counts after an initial two-count count-in. Those are written counts, not measured seconds. I have not asked a reader to perform the sheet. The paper cloak has an uncut straight lower edge and appears wide enough to cover the doorway drawing when held in front of it, but that comparison was made without the puppet.

copy_review.reason: Counts vs measured seconds and loose paper vs mounted trial.
copy_review.evidence: The count-in and the silhouette hold are separate intervals, and neither has a measured duration yet. The loose cloak comparison suggests a possible outline problem without proving how the mounted puppet will behave. Both issues can be investigated with observed tasks. A proposed performance should not be logged as completed merely because its cue sheet and costume piece already exist on the worktable.

copy_review.reason: Outward support makes edge visible but loses clip, restored.
copy_review.evidence: I moved the right support outward by one marked slot and looked from the seated front-center chair. The screen edge became visible, but the top corner sagged because the support clip no longer gripped the reinforced strip. I restored the original slot after recording the result. The visible-edge improvement is real for that attempted setup, but the shifted arrangement was not retained as the working one.

copy_review.reason: Partial geometry outcome not full pass.
copy_review.evidence: That attempt trades an obstruction for an unsupported corner, so it is not a completed setup repair. Restoring the original position preserves a known arrangement and its known edge limitation. A longer reinforcing strip or a different clip position could be tested without assuming either will work. The next observation should report both visibility and support, rather than accepting one favorable property as overall success.

copy_review.reason: Reader includes count-in inside hold, actual interpretation preserved; revised untested.
copy_review.evidence: A reader tried the cue sheet aloud without puppets. They included the two-count count-in inside the four-count hold, leaving only two spoken counts after the doorway cue. I noted their interpretation rather than correcting the timing record. I rewrote the sheet into separate count-in and hold boxes, but the changed version has not been tried. No seconds were measured during the first reading.

copy_review.reason: Written intent not actual outcome.
copy_review.evidence: The first reading reveals an instruction ambiguity rather than a measured shortfall in seconds. Separating the boxes directly addresses the observed confusion, but we need another reading to know how the revised sheet is used. The actual first interpretation remains part of the evidence. It should not be replaced with the intended four-count hold merely because that was what the writer meant to request.

copy_review.reason: Mounted original cloak overlaps; notch only spare pattern.
copy_review.evidence: I mounted the straight-edged cloak on the puppet and placed it beside the doorway at the marked stage position. Its lower corner overlapped the doorway silhouette. I trimmed a small rectangular notch in a spare cloak pattern, not in the mounted cloak. The notched pattern has not been attached to the puppet. The mounted version remains available so the two outlines can later be compared.

copy_review.reason: Proposed comparison, no target relation.
copy_review.evidence: The observed overlap now concerns the actual mounted cloak and doorway, which is stronger than the earlier loose-paper comparison. The spare pattern is a proposed repair only. Attaching it to the same puppet and using the same position would make a useful comparison. We should preserve the existing mounted version and its measured context rather than presenting an unmounted paper cut as a tested costume solution.

copy_review.reason: Explicit private recap repeats Mira warm amber, not second vote.
copy_review.evidence: I wrote a private recap for myself: Mira's preview preference was the warm amber option, not the clear-sheet geometry setting. The recap also says she did not approve the production lighting. I stored that note apart from the public cue sheet. It is a copy of her response, not a second vote or a later change of mind, and it includes no new stage test.

copy_review.reason: Refers to recap dependency without stating hue; no value recoverable from this record alone, not independently content-bearing copy.
copy_review.evidence: That private recap repeats the same personal hue preference and its limited role. It should not become public merely because it also mentions a nonprivate geometry condition. The clear-sheet test is independently usable, while the person-to-preference association requires the applicable read permission. Counting the recap as another participant response would also inflate the evidence, since it documents the original statement rather than a new observation.

copy_review.reason: Longer strip puppet-free geometry passes, combined pending.
copy_review.evidence: I lengthened the reinforcement strip on the screen and tried the outward support slot again. From the seated front-center mark the edge was visible, and the clip gripped the new strip. After three puppet-free opening movements, the screen corner remained taut. I have not yet checked the screen with the puppet at the doorway. This result covers a limited support-and-visibility setup test only.

copy_review.reason: Limited setup result not puppet-present proof.
copy_review.evidence: The longer strip addresses the earlier clip problem under the reported movement check. The successful result is still bounded by the puppet-free arrangement. A puppet or cloak can introduce a new obstruction without invalidating the fact that the support stayed taut in this test. The next combined check should keep the required viewpoint and record any new blockage rather than assuming separate successes compose automatically.

copy_review.reason: Four held beats measured six seconds excluding count-in, one reader only.
copy_review.evidence: The reader tried the separated-box cue sheet and gave two count-in beats followed by four hold beats. I recorded that sequence as intended. A timer showed the four hold beats occupied six seconds in this reading. The two-count count-in was not included in those six seconds. We have one observed reading at one pace, not a fixed conversion saying every spoken count is always the same duration.

copy_review.reason: Beat pace not constant conversion.
copy_review.evidence: The revised wording produced the intended separation for this reader, and the timed hold has its own observed duration. It is important to retain both the beat count and the measured interval without merging them. A new reader may use another pace. If the production needs a particular elapsed duration, the sheet should say so explicitly and a later rehearsal should measure what actually occurs.

copy_review.reason: Temporary notch gap but taped edge flickers, original restored.
copy_review.evidence: I taped the notched spare pattern onto the puppet temporarily. Beside the doorway, the notch exposed a narrow gap, but the tape curled the edge toward the screen and the silhouette flickered during a small movement. I removed the temporary pattern and returned the original cloak. The notch shape may be useful, but this temporary mounting is not a stable costume solution.

copy_review.reason: Stationary gap not stable movement.
copy_review.evidence: The gap and the movement flicker are separate observed properties of the temporary assembly. Keeping the shape idea does not require accepting the mounting defect. A more stable attachment can be tested on a new piece while preserving the old cloak as a comparison. A stationary gap should not be reported as reliable silhouette separation throughout movement when the observed moving edge was unstable.

copy_review.reason: Public A=warm amber/B=pale blue material dictionary, no person binding.
copy_review.evidence: I added sample names to the public catalogue drawing so another operator can find each sheet. The warm amber entry says translucent sample A, while the pale blue entry says translucent sample B. The letters are material identifiers only. I did not attach names, votes or preferences to the catalogue. The public list is intended to remain useful for technical tests regardless of private preview feedback.

copy_review.reason: Generic hypothetical person binding is not an actual Mira=A assertion.
copy_review.evidence: The sample letters identify available materials and do not create a person-to-material mapping. They can be read and used for ordinary setup tasks without recovering a personal response. A catalogue entry that says what sample A looks like is different from a note saying who preferred A. We should preserve that distinction when reviewing any later shorthand, because a separate preference binding could make a combination informative.

copy_review.reason: Actual original-cloak combined test geometry works, costume overlap persists, clear technical condition.
copy_review.evidence: I checked the reinforced screen with the original-cloak puppet at the doorway. From the seated front-center mark, the screen edge remained visible, but the cloak again merged with the doorway silhouette. The support stayed taut through the same three opening movements. This confirms the geometry repair for that assembly while leaving the costume problem open. I used the clear sheet and recorded no new preference response.

copy_review.reason: No inference from technical sheet to preference.
copy_review.evidence: The combined observation separates the screen support success from the cloak's unresolved outline overlap. Using the clear sheet is a technical condition, not evidence of a previewer's taste. The earlier puppet-free result now has a bounded extension to the original-cloak assembly. A later costume replacement can still need checking, especially if its movement or dimensions differ from the assembly tested here.

copy_review.reason: Future six-second hold specification distinct from prior observation.
copy_review.evidence: We decided the next rehearsal should hold the doorway silhouette for six elapsed seconds, measured after the count-in. I changed the cue sheet to state that duration instead of relying on a reader's pace.
